# TSD: Contentful Integration - SFCC-Side Design & Content Model ## Document Information | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Document ID** | TSD-SFCC-249 | | **Author(s)** | Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz - Squad-A (source draft). Reformatted by Marcel Angelo Navarro - Squad-A (Front-End Lead). | | **Reviewer(s)** | Jasmijn Tsang - BA Lead; Tim Lavelle - Solution Architect | | **Created** | 22 Jul 2026 (source draft). Reformat draft: 31 Jul 2026. | | **Version** | v0.1 - Draft (reformat of source v30) | | **Status** | Draft - for review, not approved for implementation | | **Related Jira** | SFCC-123 (original spike, Done); SFCC-249 (review, feedback and sign-off, Code Review) | --- ## Version History | Version | Date | Summary of Change | Author | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v0.1 | 31 Jul 2026 | Reformatted source page 346783750 (v30) into the prescribed 8-section TSD template (best-fit). Corrections applied (see file header). Open items carried to Section 7. | Marcel Angelo Navarro | *Full content history for the source page is on Confluence (346783750).* --- ## 1. Problem Statement ### 1.1 Context Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards. ### 1.2 Problem Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards. ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build. ### 1.4 Success Criteria 1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue. 2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories. 3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined. 4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners. 5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy. *These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.* --- ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions ### 2.1 Constraints | Constraint | Detail | | --- | --- | | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | | Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. | | Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). | | Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. | | Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts and 9 Contentful locales (serving 11 storefront-locale URL routes across 10 PWA sites). No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and the REG-005 risk in Section 7. | | Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. | ### 2.2 Assumptions | Assumption | Risk if Wrong | | --- | --- | | Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. | | The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). | | US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement but is not yet in Business Manager or the routing config (`sites.overlay.js`). | If it lands before bootstrap it may add a 10th Contentful locale and change the built SFCC-site count. Tracked in Section 7. | | Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. | | The Contentful account is on the Enterprise plan. | If not, the production alias (zero-downtime releases) is unavailable. | --- ## 3. Options Analysis > The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document. ### 3.1 Options Summary | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync).
+ SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash).
+ Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.
+ The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - Authors enter a raw ID with no referential-integrity check against the live catalogue (typo risk).
- SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages.
- Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) | | **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift).
- Couples the two systems.
- Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected | | **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash).
- Ships unneeded entries to the browser.
- Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No | > **Honesty note:** the source design documents Option A as the resolved approach; Options B and C are recorded here as the genuine design space, not as alternatives that were formally weighed. The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app is closer to Option B for the authoring step, and its field/payload shape (and therefore whether A's plain-ShortText choice survives) is the subject of SFCC-238. ### 3.2 Option Detail #### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5. #### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected) Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume. #### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)* Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components. --- ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale ### 4.1 Recommended Option **Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.** ### 4.2 Rationale Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238. ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted - Authors enter SFCC IDs by hand with no referential-integrity guardrail (typo risk). The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app may improve the authoring step; the field mechanic is confirmed by SFCC-238. - Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages. - This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5). --- ## 5. Technical Implementation ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow) 1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X). 2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). 3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type. 4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component. 5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output). 6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated). 7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys. > **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live. ### 5.2 Component / API Changes | File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New | | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified | | `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New | | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified | | `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified | | GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New | > Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**. ### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces **Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields): | Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. | | `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. | | `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. | | `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. | **Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert): ```js { id: 'sfccCategoryId', name: 'SFCC Category ID', type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI localized: false, required: false, validations: [], } ``` **MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):** ```js const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({ content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert', locale: currentLocale, }); const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => { const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields; // null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; }); // Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component return ; ``` **Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. **Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages. ### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases | Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error | | Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case | | Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error | | Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case | | Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error | | Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case | | Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case | > **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7. ### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes **Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve **11 storefront-locale URL routes** across **10 PWA sites and 8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). US-International (REG-005) is not yet configured (Section 7). **Token boundary.** | Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. | | CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. | | CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Build-time only; never in MRT/bundle. | | Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). | **Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one: - **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`, generated from `@cf` JSDoc): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route. - **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide. - **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component. - Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. lines: **Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:

-- **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`, generated from `@cf` JSDoc): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.

+- **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.

- **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.
- **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.

- Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.

I have now verified all citations against the live systems. Here is my complete, skeptical audit.

## Audit findings: SFCC-249 reformat draft vs live Confluence/Jira (space SFCC)

### 1. Confluence page IDs resolve correctly — ALL CONFIRMED
Every cited page ID resolves, and the draft's titles match:
- **318472193** → "Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" (v10). Draft's "runbook" label correct.
- **256835585** → "Technical Solution Design – PWA" (v11). Has a real **§12.1 "Blast-Radius Containment"** with the Contentful/dispatcher bullet the draft cites. Confirmed.
- **292061208** → "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (v9). Correct.
- **303071234** → "04.1.1 Homepage and Content" (v14), contains HPC-001. Correct.
- **303104002** → "04.1.6 Regional Storefronts" (v13), contains REG-001/005/043. Correct.
- **302186497** → "DC002 - Product Images Location" (v3) — **body is genuinely empty** (metadata only). Draft's "DC002 empty" is accurate.
- Source **346783750** = "Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model (SFCC-249)", **version 30** — draft header's "v30" is correct.
- Template **352419841** = "Technical Solution Document (TSD) Template" (v2) — confirms the 8-section structure and 7-field Document Information the draft mirrors.

### 2. HPC-001 usage — CONFIRMED CORRECT
HPC-001 verbatim: "serve all homepage content from Contentful as the sole CMS across all regional storefronts" (Confirmed). The draft cites HPC-001 only for "Contentful is the sole CMS" (§2.1) — consistent with how runbook 318472193 itself cites it. The draft does **not** pin the "connector app / resolved at render" claim to HPC-001 (that sits in §2.2/§4.3 assumptions and is routed to SFCC-238). Correct handling.

### 3. REG counts — mostly DEFENSIBLE, but one sub-claim conflicts with two TSDs
- REG-043 verbatim: "11 active locales across 7 storefronts" — draft's **11 routes** and **9 Contentful locales** are correct (runbook 318472193 lists exactly 9 locales: en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE). "en-GB shared by UK + EU-domestic-English" matches the runbook.
- REG-001 body: "7 independent storefronts… each configured as a separate site"; comment: **"Confirmed 8 storefronts."** REG-005 body: US dom + intl "**within the same site**"; comment: **"8 storefronts (US International and Domestic separate)."** So the draft's "**8 storefronts / 7 SFCC BM sites**" reconciliation is well-grounded in the REG source of truth, and **REG-005 is handled correctly** (reuses en-US + the US SFCC site → no new locale/site; status Confirmed).
- **FLAG (most material):** The draft states "8 storefronts resolve to **7 SFCC Business Manager sites**" as a flat fact in a Constraints table (§2.1) and §5.5. This **directly contradicts two other live TSDs**: PWA TSD 256835585 §5.1 ("**8 independent SFCC sites**… US/EU domestic and international are configured as **separate SFCC sites**") and Product TSD 292061208 §5/§9 (lists **ZimmermannUS and ZimmermannUSIntl as separate sites** with separate storefront catalogues; "one master + **eight** storefront catalogues"). The draft flags REG-005 as a config-consistency open item in §7 but never names this specific 7-vs-8-site contradiction with the PWA/Product TSDs. A reviewer can legitimately challenge the "7 sites" assertion. (Note: PWA TSD even mis-cites "REG-006" for the US split, when US is REG-005 — so the source material is itself inconsistent.)

### 4. Every Jira key → title/type/status — CONFIRMED (with minor label notes)
All keys resolve with the stated type/status:
- **Epics confirmed:** SFCC-10 "Z.immerse", SFCC-11 "Cart & Inventory", SFCC-12 "Checkout Flow & Delivery", SFCC-14 "Returns & Refunds" — all Epic. Draft's "(Epic)" tags correct.
- **SFCC-67** = "Contentful CMS in Checkout", **Story, parent = SFCC-12** (Checkout epic). Exactly as draft states. Confirmed.
- **SFCC-123** Spike/**Done**; **SFCC-249** Spike/**Code Review** (reporter Hazel Marie Cacalda, assignee Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz). Both confirmed.
- Sprint-1/2 cards all confirmed: SFCC-51 "Promotional Announcement Banner UI" **Blocked** ✓, 111 "…— Contentful", 55 "Global Footer UI", 117 "…— Contentful", 90 "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI", 58 "Home Page Contentful Integration", 94 "Homepage Content Row — Flexible Grid & Image Carousel", 96 "Navigation Menu — Desktop Mega Menu", 52 "Global Header UI", 82 "PLP – Bottom Zone…" (Ready For Review), 203, 190/269/273 (Grid Insert variants) + 204 (Contentful), 195 "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care" (+267/266/102/101), 173, 160, 162.
- **Minor label/mapping notes (defensible, not errors):**
  - SFCC-11's real title is "Cart & Inventory" (draft's row label is the content type "Mini-cart Shop the Look" under that epic).
  - SFCC-52 is "Global Header UI" (**also Blocked**) — draft groups it under "Navigation / Mega Menu"; SFCC-55 is **also Blocked**. Draft only annotates SFCC-51 as Blocked.
  - SFCC-102 is "PDP – Slide Out - Size & Fit" (draft labels it "Size Guide").
  - **Terminology:** Jira calls the PDP tabs "**Slide Out**" (195/267/266/102/101); the draft calls them "**PDP accordion**" (§5.4/§7/Appx C). Same feature, different word.

### 5. SFCC-238 vs SFCC-237 routing — CONFIRMED
- **SFCC-238** = "Spike: Contentful-to-PWA Kit Product/Category ID Rendering (**Hook Integration**)" (Ready for Development) = reference-resolution/hook wiring. Draft routes reference-resolution here and explicitly notes it does **not** cover PLP pagination. Correct.
- **SFCC-237** = "Spike: MRT Application Architecture Strategy" (In Progress) = MRT app architecture. Draft routes this correctly (§8, References). Correct.

### 6. The two "uncarded" spikes — CONFIRMED STILL UNCARDED
I listed all 17 SFCC spikes and text-searched summaries for pagination/item-count/grid-injection/accordion/mixed-content:
- **No spike** covers PLP grid-injection **pagination/item-count**. Confirmed uncarded.
- **No spike** covers **PDP accordion mixed content** (Contentful + SFCC tabs) rendering mechanism. Confirmed uncarded. (The only near-hits are SFCC-207, a **Done subtask** "Ask Charmaine on how accordion tabs work in desktop design" — a design-fit question, not the rendering mechanism — and SFCC-287, a cart-page accordion Story. Neither cards the draft's open item.) Draft's §7 claim is accurate.

### 7. Sign-off / Document Information — CONFIRMED
- SFCC-249 **reporter = Hazel Marie Cacalda** ✓; **author/assignee = Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz** ✓ (also SFCC-123 assignee).
- Roles: Jasmijn Tsang and Tim Lavelle are both active users and their roles (BA Lead / Solution Architect) are consistent with project context (Tsang reports most epics/stories; Lavelle is the named decision-maker across the Confluence docs). Role *titles* aren't stamped on issue metadata, but nothing contradicts them.
- Draft **Document Information now has exactly the 7 template fields** (Document ID, Author(s), Reviewer(s), Created, Version, Status, Related Jira) and **no "Contributors" row** — matches template 352419841. Confirmed.

### 8. CMA-token state — CONFIRMED, §7 row is fair
Runbook 318472193 **Human Setup Checklist item 9** ("Add CI service account CMA token as CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN GitHub Actions secret") **still reads "incomplete."** (Item 1, "generate the CMA token," reads complete — so token generated, secret not yet stored, per the runbook.) The draft's §7 row accurately represents runbook-says-incomplete vs draft-says-Complete. The "confirmed by Tim, 23 Jul" attribution is internal to the draft and not independently verifiable from the pages, but the documented inconsistency is real and fairly stated.

### 9. CPA doc-inconsistency flag — CONFIRMED ACCURATE
- Runbook 318472193: "Contentful Preview API (CPA) **available server-side only**"; token table "**server-side only.**"
- PWA TSD 256835585 §7.2: CPA "**held server-side and proxied through MRT** — never reaches the browser" (MRT-mediated); §4.1 repeats "proxied server-side; never reaches the browser."
Both pages do describe CPA as server-side/MRT-proxied, so the draft's §7 flag (that these two docs are stale vs its own decided client-side Live-Preview design) is accurate.

### Additional / lower-severity notes
- **§7 "MRT env vars per tier (4 of 9)"** — the "4 of 9" quantity is **not derivable from the cited runbook** (318472193 item 4 just reads "incomplete"; its tables list 6 tiers and 6 Contentful env vars, no "9"). Likely sourced from the codebase/source page; flagged as unverifiable against the cited Confluence page.
- **§7 "SFCC-162 … Could Have"** — SFCC-162's Jira **priority is Medium** and it's Unassigned; "Could Have" (MoSCoW) isn't in the priority field (may be in labels/description). Minor.
- The draft's §12.1 dispatcher nuance (contentful v11 SDK is axios-based, exposes httpsAgent/httpAgent/adapter, not undici's dispatcher) accurately represents what PWA TSD §12.1 says ("does not expose a `dispatcher` hook… connection isolation not achievable") and correctly routes the correction to the PWA TSD owner rather than restating it.

**Bottom line:** No fabricated page IDs or Jira keys; every citation resolves and every asserted type/status matches. The one substantive accuracy caveat is the **"7 SFCC Business Manager sites"** claim (§2.1/§5.5): defensible from REG-001/REG-005 but in **direct conflict with PWA TSD 256835585 and Product TSD 292061208 (both = 8 separate SFCC sites)**, and the draft doesn't name that cross-TSD conflict. Everything else is accurate, with only minor label/terminology mismatches in the Appendix C content-type→Jira mapping.

Marcel Angelo Navarro - Squad-A Front-End Lead (technical review; restructure; validation and corrections; open-item triage). | 25 | **Reviewer(s)** | Jasmijn Tsang - BA Lead; Tim Lavelle - Solution Architect | 26 | **Created** | 22 Jul 2026 (source draft). Reformat draft: 31 Jul 2026. | 27 | **Version** | v0.1 - Draft (reformat of source v30) | 28 | **Status** | Draft - for review, not approved for implementation | 29 | **Related Jira** | SFCC-123 (original spike, Done); SFCC-249 (review, feedback and sign-off, Code Review) | 30 31 --- 32 33 ## Version History 34 35 | Version | Date | Summary of Change | Author | 36 | --- | --- | --- | --- | 37 | v0.1 | 31 Jul 2026 | Restructured source page 346783750 (v30) into the prescribed 8-section TSD template - and, beyond a format pass: (a) corrected the preview-token boundary to the decided client-side Live Preview design (PR #41/#43); (b) reconciled the locale and storefront counts against the codebase and the PRD; (c) scoped the SFCC-ID pattern as the single design decision and routed reference-resolution to SFCC-238; (d) established the Studio Experiences vs coded-component authoring rule; (e) verified every factual claim against the codebase, Confluence and Jira; (f) captured all owner-pending items in Section 7 with owners. | Marcel Angelo Navarro | 38 39 *This revision is a technical review and restructure, not only a reformat. The substantive changes are itemised above and in the file header; each was validated against source. Full content history for the source page is on Confluence (346783750).* 40 41 --- 42 43 ## 1. Problem Statement 44 45 ### 1.1 Context 46 47 Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards. 48 49 ### 1.2 Problem 50 51 Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards. 52 53 ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved 54 55 Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build. 56 57 ### 1.4 Success Criteria 58 59 1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue. 60 2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories. 61 3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined. 62 4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners. 63 5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy. 64 65 *These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.* 66 67 --- 68 69 ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions 70 71 ### 2.1 Constraints 72 73 | Constraint | Detail | 74 | --- | --- | 75 | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | 76 | Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. | 77 | Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). | 78 | Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. | 79 | Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. | 80 | Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. | 81 82 ### 2.2 Assumptions 83 84 | Assumption | Risk if Wrong | 85 | --- | --- | 86 | Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. | 87 | The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). | 88 | US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement (a Global-e-owned international checkout path for the US) but is not yet wired in the codebase: it is a filtered-out configuration stub, planned as its own SFCC site (`ZimmermannUSIntl`), with its locale not yet assigned. | When wired it becomes the 8th wired SFCC site and may add a 10th Contentful locale. Confirm scope and timing with the regional-config owner before bootstrap. Tracked in Section 7. | 89 | Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. | 90 | The Contentful account is on the Enterprise plan. | If not, the production alias (zero-downtime releases) is unavailable. | 91 92 --- 93 94 ## 3. Options Analysis 95 96 > The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document. 97 98 ### 3.1 Options Summary 99 100 | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | 101 | --- | --- | --- | --- | 102 | **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync).
+ SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash).
+ Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.
+ The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - Authors enter a raw ID with no referential-integrity check against the live catalogue (typo risk).
- SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages.
- Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) | 103 | **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift).
- Couples the two systems.
- Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected | 104 | **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash).
- Ships unneeded entries to the browser.
- Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No | 105 ### 3.2 Option Detail 106 107 #### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering 108 109 SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5. 110 111 #### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected) 112 113 Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume. 114 115 #### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)* 116 117 Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components. 118 119 --- 120 121 ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale 122 123 ### 4.1 Recommended Option 124 125 **Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.** 126 127 ### 4.2 Rationale 128 129 Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238. 130 131 ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted 132 133 - Authors enter SFCC IDs by hand with no referential-integrity guardrail (typo risk). The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app may improve the authoring step; the field mechanic is confirmed by SFCC-238. 134 - Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages. 135 - This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5). 136 137 --- 138 139 ## 5. Technical Implementation 140 141 ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow) 142 143 1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X). 144 2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). 145 3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type. 146 4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component. 147 5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output). 148 6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated). 149 7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys. 150 151 > **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live. 152 153 ### 5.2 Component / API Changes 154 155 | File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type | 156 | --- | --- | --- | 157 | MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New | 158 | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified | 159 | `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New | 160 | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified | 161 | `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified | 162 | GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New | 163 164 > Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**. 165 166 ### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces 167 168 **Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields): 169 170 | Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description | 171 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 172 | `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. | 173 | `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. | 174 | `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. | 175 | `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. | 176 177 **Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert): 178 179 ```js 180 { 181 id: 'sfccCategoryId', 182 name: 'SFCC Category ID', 183 type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI 184 localized: false, 185 required: false, 186 validations: [], 187 } 188 ``` 189 190 **MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):** 191 192 ```js 193 const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({ 194 content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert', 195 locale: currentLocale, 196 }); 197 198 const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => { 199 const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields; 200 // null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render 201 return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; 202 }); 203 204 // Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component 205 return ; 206 ``` 207 208 **Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. 209 210 **Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages. 211 212 ### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases 213 214 | Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type | 215 | --- | --- | --- | 216 | Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error | 217 | Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case | 218 | Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error | 219 | Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case | 220 | Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error | 221 | Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case | 222 | Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case | 223 224 > **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7. 225 226 ### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes 227 228 **Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7. 229 230 **Token boundary.** 231 232 | Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes | 233 | --- | --- | --- | --- | 234 | CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. | 235 | CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. | 236 | CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Build-time only; never in MRT/bundle. | 237 | Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). | 238 239 **Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one: 240 241 - **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route. 242 - **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide. 243 - **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component. 244 - Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice. 245 246 --- 247 248 ## 6. Testing & Validation 249 250 ### 6.1 Test Coverage 251 252 This spike produces findings and a design, not a testable build; the tests below belong to the downstream build stories. 253 254 | Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria | 255 | --- | --- | --- | 256 | Validation of findings (this spike) | The design cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence (maps to Section 1.4). | Every design claim traces to a verified source; current-versus-target state is stated honestly. | 257 | Unit (downstream) | SSR-side SFCC-ID filter; presentation-only component renders pre-filtered entries and null-returns on empty. | Filter selects matching + null-ID entries only; component holds no ID logic. | 258 | Integration (downstream) | SSR cache key includes the SFCC ID; publish webhook purges the correct keys. | No cross-page editorial bleed; content updates appear after publish within the SWR window. | 259 | E2E / Playwright (downstream) | Editorial content renders on the scoped category/product page and not elsewhere. | Observable in the UI across representative storefronts. | 260 261 ### 6.2 Regression Risk 262 263 Low today: the reformatted design does not change running code. The material regression surface arrives with the downstream build, concentrated on two points that the build stories must cover explicitly: **SSR ID-filter correctness** and **cache-key isolation** (a wrong or missing key leaks editorial content across pages). 264 265 --- 266 267 ## 7. # TSD: Contentful Integration - SFCC-Side Design & Content Model ## Document Information | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Document ID** | TSD-SFCC-249 | | **Author(s)** | Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz - Squad-A (original spike draft, SFCC-123). Marcel Angelo Navarro - Squad-A Front-End Lead (technical review; restructure; validation and corrections; open-item triage). | | **Reviewer(s)** | Jasmijn Tsang - BA Lead; Tim Lavelle - Solution Architect | | **Created** | 22 Jul 2026 (source draft). Reformat draft: 31 Jul 2026. | | **Version** | v0.1 - Draft (reformat of source v30) | | **Status** | Draft - for review, not approved for implementation | | **Related Jira** | SFCC-123 (original spike, Done); SFCC-249 (review, feedback and sign-off, Code Review) | --- ## Version History | Version | Date | Summary of Change | Author | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v0.1 | 31 Jul 2026 | Restructured source page 346783750 (v30) into the prescribed 8-section TSD template - and, beyond a format pass: (a) corrected the preview-token boundary to the decided client-side Live Preview design (PR #41/#43); (b) reconciled the locale and storefront counts against the codebase and the PRD; (c) scoped the SFCC-ID pattern as the single design decision and routed reference-resolution to SFCC-238; (d) established the Studio Experiences vs coded-component authoring rule; (e) verified every factual claim against the codebase, Confluence and Jira; (f) captured all owner-pending items in Section 7 with owners. | Marcel Angelo Navarro | *This revision is a technical review and restructure, not only a reformat. The substantive changes are itemised above and in the file header; each was validated against source. Full content history for the source page is on Confluence (346783750).* --- ## 1. Problem Statement ### 1.1 Context Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards. ### 1.2 Problem Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards. ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build. ### 1.4 Success Criteria 1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue. 2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories. 3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined. 4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners. 5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy. *These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.* --- ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions ### 2.1 Constraints | Constraint | Detail | | --- | --- | | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | | Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. | | Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). | | Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. | | Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. | | Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. | ### 2.2 Assumptions | Assumption | Risk if Wrong | | --- | --- | | Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. | | The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). | | US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement (a Global-e-owned international checkout path for the US) but is not yet wired in the codebase: it is a filtered-out configuration stub, planned as its own SFCC site (`ZimmermannUSIntl`), with its locale not yet assigned. | When wired it becomes the 8th wired SFCC site and may add a 10th Contentful locale. Confirm scope and timing with the regional-config owner before bootstrap. Tracked in Section 7. | | Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. | | The Contentful account is on the Enterprise plan. | If not, the production alias (zero-downtime releases) is unavailable. | --- ## 3. Options Analysis > The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document. ### 3.1 Options Summary | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync).
+ SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash).
+ Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.
+ The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - Authors enter a raw ID with no referential-integrity check against the live catalogue (typo risk).
- SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages.
- Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) | | **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift).
- Couples the two systems.
- Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected | | **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash).
- Ships unneeded entries to the browser.
- Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No | ### 3.2 Option Detail #### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5. #### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected) Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume. #### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)* Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components. --- ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale ### 4.1 Recommended Option **Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.** ### 4.2 Rationale Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238. ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted - Authors enter SFCC IDs by hand with no referential-integrity guardrail (typo risk). The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app may improve the authoring step; the field mechanic is confirmed by SFCC-238. - Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages. - This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5). --- ## 5. Technical Implementation ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow) 1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X). 2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). 3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type. 4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component. 5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output). 6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated). 7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys. > **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live. ### 5.2 Component / API Changes | File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New | | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified | | `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New | | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified | | `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified | | GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New | > Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**. ### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces **Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields): | Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. | | `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. | | `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. | | `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. | **Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert): ```js { id: 'sfccCategoryId', name: 'SFCC Category ID', type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI localized: false, required: false, validations: [], } ``` **MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):** ```js const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({ content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert', locale: currentLocale, }); const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => { const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields; // null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; }); // Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component return ; ``` **Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. **Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages. ### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases | Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error | | Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case | | Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error | | Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case | | Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error | | Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case | | Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case | > **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7. ### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes **Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7. **Token boundary.** | Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. | | CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. | | CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Build-time only; never in MRT/bundle. | | Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). | **Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one: - **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route. - **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide. - **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Overview

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime - Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

Direction

Flow

Inbound (Contentful → MRT)

Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). Target: fetched server-side by the MRT SSR layer. Current: fetched client-side post-hydration.

Outbound (MRT → Contentful)

Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful.

NOT in this flow

SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager.

Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.

Integration Architecture & Data Flow

Pattern: Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser.

SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized - they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

Field Name

Field Type

Localized

Applies To

Description

No

The SFCC category ID (e.g. womens-dresses) this entry is scoped to. If null, the entry is shown on all categories of that type.

Short Text

No

The SFCC product ID (master product ID) this entry is scoped to. If null, shown on all PDPs.
