Authoring rule: content authors set sfccCategoryId / sfccProductId in Contentful. They do not need to know anything about how MRT resolves it - that logic lives entirely in the SSR layer.

Schema-as-Code Definition

Each content type that supports ID-based targeting must include the relevant field in its scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js definition. Example for PLP Inline Grid Insert:

wide760true

Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries - it receives only the entries that should render.

Resolution logic by page context:

Page Context

ID Source

Match Logic

PLP (category page)

Route param / SFCC category API response

Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all).

PDP (product page)

Route param productId (master product ID)

Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null.

Homepage

No SFCC ID context

No ID filtering - all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order.

Campaign landing

Slug / experience ID

Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience - no SFCC ID filtering needed.

Pseudocode - MRT SSR filter (PLP example):

const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;

Cache Key Requirements

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category. 

Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.

locale + productId

locale only (no SFCC ID context)

Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

  • The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries - it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.

  • The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.

  • The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.

  • If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing - null return, no DOM output.

This keeps the component reusable across different SFCC ID scopes without modification.

Null / Unscoped Behaviour

A Contentful entry with sfccCategoryId = null (field left empty by the author) is treated as "show on all categories" for that content type. This is the default authoring state. Authors only populate the ID field when they want to restrict the component to a specific category or product.

Environment & Locale Configuration

The platform uses a single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev → test → sit → staging → uat → production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias (CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production) for zero-downtime releases. Nine locales are configured across eight storefronts, with en as the default fallback. Full environment setup, alias management, and locale configuration are maintained in Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations.

Locale Rules for Content Modellers

  • Translatable fields (headline, body copy, CTA text, alt text) → set localized: true in the content type definition.

  • Structural fields (asset links, layout flags, product IDs) → set localized: false - shared across all locales. Canonical examples of non-localized structural fields: sfccCategoryId and sfccProductId. These are SFCC identifiers and do not vary by locale.

  • Fallback chain: if a locale (e.g. fr) has no content for a field, Contentful falls back to en automatically. Authors only fill fields they want to override.

  • Translation pipeline: Transperfect is the translation partner (HPC-006). Strategy is under discussion - Contentful squad to own.

Key Design Decisions

Decision

Choice

Rationale

Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts

One Space, per-locale content fields

Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication and reduces operational overhead vs one space per storefront.

Schema as code - not hand-created in UI

Git-managed definitions deployed via npm run sync:contentful

Prevents schema drift, enables code review of content model changes, and gives CI visibility of structural changes before production.

CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only)

Delivery API token is browser-safe

CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. Preview (CPA) and Management (CMA) tokens are never deployed to MRT or exposed to the browser.

Production alias instead of fixed environment name

CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production resolves to an alias

Enables zero-downtime releases: flip the alias to a pre-tested release clone without redeploying MRT. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan.

ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish

Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook → MRT invalidates cache

Pages are server-rendered and cached. Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until cache TTL expires. Webhook makes updates near-real-time.

Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability

Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down

Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. Editorial content is an enhancement, not a dependency.

Contentful SDK v11 - no connection pool isolation hook

Mitigate via graceful degradation, not pool isolation

SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. Primary mitigation is graceful degradation.

SFCC ID references in Contentful content model

Plain ShortText fields (sfccProductId, sfccCategoryId), localized: false. Filtering in MRT SSR, not in the React component.

ID fields are structural, not editorial - they do not vary by locale. Resolution and conditional rendering happen entirely in the MRT SSR layer. The Contentful entry is the editorial shell; SFCC provides the commerce data it wraps. Components remain dumb and reusable. Cache keys must include the SFCC ID to avoid cross-context cache collisions.

## Document Information | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Document ID** | TSD-SFCC-249 | | **Author(s)** | Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz - Squad-A (original spike draft, SFCC-123). Marcel Angelo Navarro - Squad-A Front-End Lead (technical review; restructure; validation and corrections; open-item triage). | | **Reviewer(s)** | Jasmijn Tsang - BA Lead; Tim Lavelle - Solution Architect | | **Created** | 22 Jul 2026 (source draft); reformatted and published as v31 on 01 Aug 2026. | | **Version** | v31 - Draft (reformatted from v30) | | **Status** | Draft - for review, not approved for implementation | | **Related Jira** | SFCC-123 (original spike, Done); SFCC-249 (review, feedback and sign-off, Code Review) | --- ## Version History | Version | Date | Summary of Change | Author | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v31 | 01 Aug 2026 | Restructured source page (v30) into the prescribed 8-section TSD template, and beyond a format pass: (a) corrected the preview-token boundary to the decided client-side Live Preview design (PR #41/#43); (b) reconciled the locale and storefront counts against the codebase and the PRD; (c) scoped the SFCC-ID pattern as the single design decision and routed reference-resolution to SFCC-238; (d) established the Studio Experiences vs coded-component authoring rule; (e) verified every factual claim against the codebase, Confluence and Jira; (f) captured all owner-pending items in Section 7 with owners. | Marcel Angelo Navarro | *This revision is a technical review and restructure, not only a reformat. The substantive changes are itemised above; each was validated against source. Prior content history (through v30) is retained in this page's Confluence version history. The document follows the prescribed TSD template (352419841), with intentional additions for this TSD: Appendices A-C carry ticket-required briefing content the single-problem template has no slot for, and the sign-off records both the BA Lead and the Solution Architect.* --- ## 1. Problem Statement ### 1.1 Context Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards. ### 1.2 Problem Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards. ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build. ### 1.4 Success Criteria 1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue. 2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories. 3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined. 4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners. 5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy. *These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.* --- ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions ### 2.1 Constraints | Constraint | Detail | | --- | --- | | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | | Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. | | Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). | | Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. | | Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. | | Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. | ### 2.2 Assumptions | Assumption | Risk if Wrong | | --- | --- | | Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. | | The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). | | US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement (a Global-e-owned international checkout path for the US) but is not yet wired in the codebase: it is a filtered-out configuration stub, planned as its own SFCC site (`ZimmermannUSIntl`), with its locale not yet assigned. | When wired it becomes the 8th wired SFCC site and may add a 10th Contentful locale. Confirm scope and timing with the regional-config owner before bootstrap. Tracked in Section 7. | | Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. | | The Contentful account is on the Enterprise plan. | If not, the production alias (zero-downtime releases) is unavailable. | --- ## 3. Options Analysis > The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document. ### 3.1 Options Summary | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync).
+ SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash).
+ Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.
+ The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - Authors enter a raw ID with no referential-integrity check against the live catalogue (typo risk).
- SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages.
- Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) | | **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift).
- Couples the two systems.
- Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected | | **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash).
- Ships unneeded entries to the browser.
- Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No | ### 3.2 Option Detail #### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5. #### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected) Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume. #### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)* Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components. --- ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale ### 4.1 Recommended Option **Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.** ### 4.2 Rationale Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238. ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted - Authors enter SFCC IDs by hand with no referential-integrity guardrail (typo risk). The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app may improve the authoring step; the field mechanic is confirmed by SFCC-238. - Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages. - This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5). --- ## 5. Technical Implementation ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow) 1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X). 2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). 3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type. 4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component. 5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output). 6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated). 7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys. > **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live. ### 5.2 Component / API Changes | File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New | | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified | | `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New | | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified | | `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified | | GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New | > Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**. ### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces **Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields): | Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. | | `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. | | `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. | | `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. | **Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert): ```js { id: 'sfccCategoryId', name: 'SFCC Category ID', type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI localized: false, required: false, validations: [], } ``` **MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):** ```js const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({ content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert', locale: currentLocale, }); const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => { const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields; // null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; }); // Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component return matchedInserts; ``` **Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. **Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages. ### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases | Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error | | Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case | | Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error | | Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case | | Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error | | Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case | | Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case | > **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7. ### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes **Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7. **Token boundary.** | Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. | | CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. | | CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Build-time only; never in MRT/bundle. | | Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). | **Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one: - **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route. - **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide. - **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component. - Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice. --- ## 6. Testing & Validation ### 6.1 Test Coverage This spike produces findings and a design, not a testable build; the tests below belong to the downstream build stories. | Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria | | --- | --- | --- | | Validation of findings (this spike) | The design cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence (maps to Section 1.4). | Every design claim traces to a verified source; current-versus-target state is stated honestly. | | Unit (downstream) | SSR-side SFCC-ID filter; presentation-only component renders pre-filtered entries and null-returns on empty. | Filter selects matching + null-ID entries only; component holds no ID logic. | | Integration (downstream) | SSR cache key includes the SFCC ID; publish webhook purges the correct keys. | No cross-page editorial bleed; content updates appear after publish within the SWR window. | | E2E / Playwright (downstream) | Editorial content renders on the scoped category/product page and not elsewhere. | Observable in the UI across representative storefronts. | ### 6.2 Regression Risk Low today: the reformatted design does not change running code. The material regression surface arrives with the downstream build, concentrated on two points that the build stories must cover explicitly: **SSR ID-filter correctness** and **cache-key isolation** (a wrong or missing key leaks editorial content across pages). --- ## 7. Risks & Mitigations > Implementation risks and open items carried to sign-off. Items owned outside Squad-A are captured with their owner and left open; this document does not resolve them. | Risk / Open Item | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Degradation stance: footer and homepage render as a broken bare page during a full CDA outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback undecided. | Med | Decide with Tim before locking; currently "risk accepted". | Tim Lavelle | | PLP grid-injection pagination / item-count not proven; no spike raised. SFCC-238 is reference-resolution and does not cover this check. | Med | Raise a spike or widen SFCC-238; mark the PLP inject "pending" until then. | Squad-A / Tim | | PDP accordion mixed content (Contentful tabs + SFCC-sourced tabs) rendering mechanism undecided; no spike raised. | Med | Raise a spike or fold into SFCC-238; SFCC-195 should not close until decided. | Squad-A / Tim | | Composed-page ownership: which PDP/PLP editorial is Contentful versus SFCC Page Designer, and mega-menu tiles, unconfirmed. Determines which content types exist. | High | Confirm with Tim and Content. | Tim / Content | | Product imagery location unresolved (PWA TSD says Contentful, Product TSD says SFCC static content library); DC002 empty. | Med | Do not assume; keep "pending DC002". | Tim / DC002 | | `regions` content-model field for cross-storefront filtering unconfirmed. | Med | Confirm with content strategy. | Content strategy | | Sprint-2 content-type field sets inferred, not confirmed. | Med | Authoring walkthrough with Emma and Dani before locking fields; keep provisional. | Emma & Dani / Tim | | Contentful Enterprise plan required for the production alias; unconfirmed. | Med | Confirm the account tier before first production release. | Zimmermann | | US-International (REG-005, Confirmed) is not yet wired in the codebase (a filtered-out config stub, planned as its own site `ZimmermannUSIntl`, locale not yet assigned). When wired it becomes the 8th SFCC site and may add a 10th Contentful locale. The PWA TSD (256835585) and Product TSD (292061208) already count 8 SFCC sites; the codebase wires 7 today. | Med | Confirm site topology, locale, and timing with the regional-config owner before bootstrap. | Regional-config owner | | New Relic not yet procured or on the credentials tracker; browser-layer ownership (Sentry versus New Relic) undecided. | Med | Procurement raised with Emma/IT (pending); frame alerts as "recommended, pending procurement". | Emma / IT | | Didomi purpose IDs for consent-gated components (Vimeo embeds) unresolved. | Med | Pending Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Vicky Routley | | Bootstrap incomplete: MRT env vars per tier (4 of 9), cache-purge webhook per env, content-type Roles restriction. | Med | Complete before the Contentful squad onboards. | Accenture / Integration Lead | | Doc inconsistency: the CMA-token GitHub Actions secret is "Complete" here (confirmed by Tim, 23 Jul) but "incomplete" in the ops runbook (318472193 item 9). | Low | Treat as Complete; the ops runbook is stale (correction is outside this document's scope). | Accenture | | Doc inconsistency: this TSD documents the CPA token as client-side (Live Preview SDK, non-prod tiers only), per the decided design (PR #41/#43 and the integration source). The Setup & Ops runbook (318472193) and PWA TSD (256835585) still describe CPA as server-side / MRT-proxied. | Low | Those two docs are stale on this point; reconciling them is outside this document's scope. Solution Architect to note the tradeoff explicitly at review. | PWA TSD / runbook owners | | PWA TSD 12.1 states Contentful connection isolation is "not achievable"; the SDK does expose `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter`. | Low | Correction belongs in PWA TSD 12.1 (its owner); this document links, does not restate. | PWA TSD owner | | Handoff Boundary table still marked `[FOR UPDATE]`. | Med | Tim to finalise (Appendix A). | Tim Lavelle | --- ## 8. content.text:
Here's the breakdown of what Tim's message actually asks for.

## The literal ask: two separate steps, in order

1. **"let's sync on it and get some of my thoughts/questions answered"** — he wants a live conversation (call/meeting), not more written review comments. He has specific questions about the v31 TSD and wants them answered directly, back-and-forth.
2. **"and then move into an actual SPIKE"** — only *after* that sync does the next phase start.
3. **"timebox to 2-3 days max"** — that next phase is tightly capped.

## The key phrase: "an actual SPIKE"

This is the important signal. SFCC-123 and SFCC-249 are both Jira-typed "Spike," but what they actually produced was a **design document** — architecture, decisions, a content-model catalogue, reviewed and reformatted. Tim calling for "an **actual** spike" is drawing a line under that: he's saying the documentation phase is done, and what happens next needs to be **hands-on technical investigation** — the classic agile-spike meaning: build something small, timeboxed, to answer a specific unresolved question, not write more design.

## Why this tracks exactly with what we just published

The v31 TSD's own §7 (Risks & Mitigations) is essentially a list of things that **can't be resolved by more writing** — they need someone to actually try it:

- **PLP grid-injection pagination/item-count** — genuinely uncarded; the only way to answer "does injecting a Contentful item break pagination" is to build and test it against a real SFCC PLP.
- **PDP accordion mixed-content rendering** — "simple SFCC var vs. dedicated component" is an implementation question, not a design question; also genuinely uncarded.
- **Option A itself is unproven** — the SFCC-ID + SSR-filter pattern is "proposed design, not yet implemented," and the Decision Record row is flagged "SA endorsement TBC." Tim may want to see it actually built end-to-end before he endorses it.
- **SFCC-238's boundary** (reference-resolution vs. these two items) may need a hands-on check too.

Any of these — or a combination — is a very plausible candidate for what Tim means by "an actual spike," and each fits a 2-3 day timebox.

## What this means for you going into the sync

- Come ready to **defend or clarify the open items**, especially the ones without an owner yet (composed-page ownership, the two uncarded spikes, Option A's endorsement).
- Expect Tim to **pick one or two concrete questions** out of §7/§8 and scope the actual spike around those — the sync is where he narrows it down, so don't assume the whole risk register becomes the spike.
- Since he's addressing both Jhoan and you, he likely wants **you and Jhoan aligned on execution** once the spike is scoped (you on the technical/SSR side, Jhoan on content-model/authoring side).

No action needed from me right now — this is purely to get you oriented before the sync. Want me to draft a short list of anticipated Tim questions pulled straight from §7/§8, so you walk in prepared?

The API is returning the old comment set from before the v31 update—I'm seeing the same 24 comment IDs from earlier, which means it's not picking up the new comments the user just added about the Global-e checkout, locale issues, and other recent feedback. This suggests the `confluence_get_comments` tool is pulling stale data rather than the updated comments. tely real, new comments on v31 that the API isn't surfacing — likely due to caching, pagination limits, or indexing delays. Since the user explicitly pasted these comments directly from Tim and my verification call returned stale data, I should treat the pasted comments as the authoritative source rather than spending more tool calls chasing an outdated API. I'll note this discrepancy for transparency but proceed with analyzing the user's pasted comments as the primary reference.

For the in-depth analysis, I'm organizing each comment into three categories: alignment items (discussions or decisions needing joint agreement), addressing items (documentation or process fixes), and actual spike work (technical build and test tasks). I'll map each comment to its anchor text and the corresponding section in the v31 TSD, then categorize it accordingly.

Starting with the first comment about Global-e's checkout ownership for the US-International requirement — this is a clarification question directed at Jasmijn Tsang asking whether Global-e handles the entire checkout path (cart, checkout, confirmation pages) or just part of it. It's a business-level requirements question rather than technical work.

The second comment about the "10th Contentful locale" is directed at Jhoan and Marcel, asking them to specify which locale code is actually being assumed as the tenth one. Tim is pushing for concrete details rather than vague references, and he's essentially highlighting the same gap we flagged in our risk section — that US-International's locale assignment is still undefined.

The third comment flags a concern about embedding specific details like Sprint-2 field sets directly in the TSD, since these can drift and require updates across multiple documents. Tim is suggesting we should consider using component requirement pages instead to capture content models and development requirements in a more maintainable way. details in the TSD creates maintenance overhead. Tim's also flagging a specific assumption about the Contentful Enterprise plan — he's saying they're already on it, so that contingency row should be removed, and he's directing this at Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz.

Moving to the next point, Tim's clarifying how the Salesforce connector handles the typo-risk concern: if an author enters a wrong product or category ID, the connector won't return any results and immediately signals to the author that the entry doesn't exist, so the referential-integrity check is actually built in. Tim's pushing back on whether the cache-key requirement was actually verified against the codebase or if it's just an unverified assumption I made — he's explicitly questioning the rigor and provenance of the technical claims in the document. He's also flagging another assertion about filtering logic being centralized in the MRT SSR layer as potentially unsubstantiated. Tim's flagging that this same concern about typo risk appears twice in the document — once in the Option A cons section and again in the Trade-offs Accepted section — so he's pointing out the duplication rather than raising a new issue.

The Component/API Changes section is where Tim sees the real work that needs to happen. He's asking what can be tackled while the MRT development approach is still being decided, since there are concrete changes needed across multiple files and endpoints — the SSR layer, the useContentful hook, webhook receiver, and schema additions — but the team hasn't settled on the overall MRT strategy yet. everything hinges on that MRT node application TSD that Marcel and Gideon are still reviewing. | v31 | 01 Aug 2026 | Restructured source page (v30) into the prescribed 8-section TSD template, and beyond a format pass: (a) corrected the preview-token boundary to the decided client-side Live Preview design (PR #41/#43); (b) reconciled the locale and storefront counts against the codebase and the PRD; (c) scoped the SFCC-ID pattern as the single design decision and routed reference-resolution to SFCC-238; (d) established the Studio Experiences vs coded-component authoring rule; (e) verified every factual claim against the codebase, Confluence and Jira; (f) captured all owner-pending items in Section 7 with owners. | Marcel Angelo Navarro |

*This revision is a technical review and restructure, not only a reformat. The substantive changes are itemised above; each was validated against source. Prior content history (through v30) is retained in this page's Confluence version history. The document follows the prescribed TSD template (352419841), with intentional additions for this TSD: Appendices A-C carry ticket-required briefing content the single-problem template has no slot for, and the sign-off records both the BA Lead and the Solution Architect.*

---

1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.

### 1.2 Problem

Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.
2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.
3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined.
4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners.
5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy.

*These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.*

---

2. Constraints & Assumptions
----------------------------

### 2.1 Constraints

| Constraint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. |
| Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |
| Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). |
| Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. |
| Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. |
| Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. |

### 2.2 Assumptions

| Assumption | Risk if Wrong |
| --- | --- |
| Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. |
| The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references; it validates against the live catalogue at authoring time, immediately showing the author when an entered ID has no match. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). |
| US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement (a Global-e-owned international checkout path for the US) but is not yet wired in the codebase: it is a filtered-out configuration stub, planned as its own SFCC site (`ZimmermannUSIntl`), with its locale not yet assigned. | When wired it becomes the 8th wired SFCC site and may add a 10th Contentful locale. Confirm scope and timing with the regional-config owner before bootstrap. Tracked in Section 7. |
| Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. |

---

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) |
| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |
| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.

#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)

Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.

#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*

Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.

---

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**

### 4.2 Rationale

Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.
* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).

---

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)

1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).
2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).
3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.
4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.
5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).
6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).
7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.

> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.

### 5.2 Component / API Changes

| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |
| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |
| `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified |
| `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified |
| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |

> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.

### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces

**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):

| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |
| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |
| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):

`{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: [],
}`

**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**

`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({
content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',
locale: currentLocale,
});
const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {
const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;
// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render
return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;
});
// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component
return matchedInserts;`

**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.

**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.

### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |
| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |
| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case |

> **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7.

### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes

**Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7.

**Token boundary.**

| Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. |

Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. |

**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:

* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.
* **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.
* **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.
* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.

content.text:
These two are a different kind of comment than 4/5/8, and that matters for what "the change" actually is.

## Why these two don't have a determinate text fix (yet)

For the connector-app correction (comments 5/8), Tim stated a fact: the connector validates IDs and shows the author immediately when nothing matches. That gave us something concrete to correct the text *to*.

For 13 and 14, Tim hasn't stated a resolution — he's raised an open question and a counter-observation:

- **#13:** *"I'm not sure we need to separate these and the components we build will most of the time being used in an experience builder."* — this is him questioning whether the two-path split (Studio Experience vs. coded content-type component) is even necessary, not telling us what to replace it with.
- **#14:** *"Authors will place elements on a page"* — this rebuts the heuristic's premise (that author-driven placement is the distinguishing signal for "Studio Experience"), by stating that author-placement is the norm, not an edge case.

Both are opinions/objections to a design decision, not corrected facts. There's no "before → after" text I can respect here without deciding, on Tim's behalf, what he actually wants the rule to become — and that's not something a document edit resolves.

## Why it's not ours to just remove or rewrite either

This rule (§5.5's Studio-Experience-vs-coded-component split) was established this session specifically by checking the actual codebase — `experiences/` uses `defineComponents` + `npm run generate:contentful`, coded components use `useContentful`, the homepage uses the coded path, `/:slug` routes to the Experience page. It's not an arbitrary preference; it describes what the two code paths actually do today. If Tim wants that categorical distinction dropped or restructured, that's a real architectural call about how future components get built — squarely the kind of decision that needs the sync conversation, not a quiet doc edit.

## What actually needs to happen

Before any text can change, the sync needs to resolve which of these Tim actually means:

- The two-path distinction stays as-is (it accurately describes current code), and the heuristic wording just needs adjusting so it doesn't conflict with "authors will place elements" — i.e. find a different distinguishing signal than "who decides placement."

contents: Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector
The Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector for Contentful allows you to use Salesforce B2C (Demandware) products and categories in your entries in Contentful. 
Overview
Link copied
Once installed, you can change the appearance for a Short Text field to load and store Salesforce Commerce Cloud product or category IDs. Your content teams can open a picker, view and search for products and categories, and embed them into an entry.
Requirements
Link copied
To use this app, you will need:

* Administrator access to Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (Demandware)
* A content type with a short text field

Usage
Link copied
Step 1: Configuring a Salesforce Commerce Cloud API Client
You will need to create a Salesforce Commerce Cloud API Client before installing the app. You can follow [Authorization for Admin APIs](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/authorization-for-admin-apis.html) to create this client.
Please copy and save the Password you select for the API Client, also known as the Client Secret.
The API Client will require you to select a list of scopes. For this app to work, your API client will need to include the following scopes at a minimum, under Allowed Scopes.
`sfcc.products`
`sfcc.catalogs`
Copy the API Client ID value and save it for later. You can now save the configuration and go to your Contentful space.
Step 2: Retrieving configuration values from your Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance
Next, you will need several values from your Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance:

* Organization ID - the unique ID for your specific Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance
* Short code - a unique value for your organization that helps route data correctly
* Site ID - the unique name of your Salesforce Commerce Cloud site

You can [follow this guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/commerce-api-configuration-values.html) to find each value. Once found, copy those values and save them for the next step.
Step 3: Installing the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector
Navigate to the Contentful Marketplace and install the Salesforce Commerce Cloud app. Upon installation, you will be asked to provide the API Client ID, Client Secret, Organization ID, Short Code and Site ID values you just generated. Provide them in the appropriate boxes of the configuration screen.
Once you've entered all of the configuration values, press Install in the top right to complete the installation of the app.
Step 4: Configure your Content Types
Once you've installed the app, you'll need to set up the content types that will be used to store the product and category information retrieved from Salesforce Commerce Cloud. Within a new or existing content type, create a new field which will be used to store the information retrieved from Salesforce Commerce Cloud by selecting the Add Field button in the right sidebar of the Content Type configuration screen, then selecting Text from the "Add new field" dialog that appears. 
When creating this field, we recommend naming it something memorable like ‘Salesforce Commerce Cloud Product’. Make sure you select the "Short text, exact search" option under type, which should be selected by default.  If you would like the field to store multiple products or categories - such as for use in a product carousel - select the List option. Select the "Add and Configure" button in the bottom right of the dialog to continue.
Next, navigate to the Appearance tab of the field editor dialog and select the Salesforce Commerce Cloud option. Once selected, choose either "Product" or "Category" from the Field Type dropdown. Finally, press Confirm to save your new field.
The last thing to do before you start using the app is to save the updated content type. Select "Save" in the top right corner and you can now start making use of the Salesforce Commerce Cloud app to select products and categories directly within your content entries.
Step 5: Selecting Products and Categories
Now that you have configured a content type, create or update an entry using that content type to begin selecting products and categories. When viewing the editor of the corresponding entry, instead of seeing the default Short Text field editor for your new field you will now see the Salesforce Commerce Cloud app interface:
Click the “Select a product” or "Select a category" button to open a dialog window for selecting the appropriate item. By default, all of your Products or Categories will load alphabetically, and a search query can also be included to narrow down the list. Depending on whether or not your Short Text field is configured as a list, you'll either have the option to select only a single item or multiple items by clicking on them in the dialog. 
After you select your item(s), press Save to embed the data into your entry. You will see a simple thumbnail for the selected product or category in the field, as well as the product name and ID. Additionally, if you selected multiple items, you can now rearrange the order of those items by dragging and dropping them into whatever order you like.

## Findings: Jira search for Experience Builder / Studio Experience direction (project SFCC)

**One clear, direct hit. Everything else came back empty or off-topic.**

### 1. The strongest piece of evidence: SFCC-51 (Promotional Announcement Banner UI)

Tim Lavelle, comment dated 2026-07-07 (comment id 13363):

> "For this being a Contenful managed element, the team needs to do a Technical Solution Design and POC on how we integrate the Business Manager properties to Contenful and call those on the component rendering. **As this will be a component in the Contenful Studio builder, users can drag-n-drop where this lives on specific pages, but if this is going to live on a PLP and/or PDP or Global across all but Zimmerse, then will likely need a configuration to target specific SFCC Category IDs and Product IDs.**"

This is significant because the Promotional Announcement Banner is explicitly **not** a Z.immerse/campaign-page component — per its own description it displays "on Home / PDP / PLP, but it does not on Z.immerse." Tim is describing it as a Studio-builder (Experience Builder), drag-and-drop component anyway. This is the one concrete instance in Jira where Tim ties Studio/Experience-Builder placement to a component living on PLP, PDP, or "Global across all but Zimmerse" — i.e., outside the Z.immerse/campaign scope.

This carried through into the accepted AC (Tim, comment 13387, same ticket):

Here are the exhaustive search results. I checked all specified terms and pages within the SFCC space; findings are grouped by search area, with page IDs and exact quotes.

## 1. Term searches: "Experience Builder," "Studio Experience," "component library," "flexible components," "page composition," "visual editor," "drag and drop," "authoring experience"

**The only substantive hits are the SFCC-249 TSD itself and its adjacent runbook.** No other page in the space discusses Experience Builder/Studio scope as a strategic or roadmap topic.

- **Page 346783750** (SFCC-249, section 5.5) — the TSD's own rule (see full quote in section 3 below): Studio Experience is scoped to "Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages"; coded components are the default for "homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide." Appendix A: "Composed pages (PDP/PLP editorial split) | All pages outside Z.immerse [Accenture builds] | Z.immerse pages [Contentful squad owns]."
- **Page 256835585** (Technical Solution Design – PWA), the only mention of "Experience Builder" outside 346783750: *"Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module."* This is a one-line implementation note about a registration mechanism — it says nothing about scope (broad vs. narrow use) and does not mention Z.immerse at all.
- **"flexible components"** appears only in **page 258801666** (04.2 Design Tracker), row for epic Z.immerse (SFCC-10): *"Immersive/editorial landing page; direct-link landing page; editorial experience components (needs definition); flexible content components"* — scoped explicitly to the Z.immerse epic, not storefront-wide.
- **"page composition," "visual editor," "drag and drop," "authoring experience"** as standalone phrases return nothing beyond the same 346783750/318472193/256835585 hits already covered — no separate strategy document uses these terms.

## 2. Z.immerse / immerse search

Every hit treats Z.immerse as a bounded, separate epic (SFCC-10), never as a template for site-wide authoring:
- **Page 258801666**: Z.immerse listed as its own epic row, sprint 4, distinct from Homepage/PLP/PDP rows.
- **Page 303071234** (HPC-024): *"The system will display a mega menu on desktop when a customer hovers over a navigation category, with the exception of Z.Immerse which will function as a direct link to a page"* — Z.immerse is explicitly called out as an exception to normal nav behavior.
- **Attachment att346750987** ("GE feedback on Zimmerman SFCC epics.xlsx"): *"Z.immerse immersive editorial experience components Native SFCC."*
- **Attachment att288849929** ("Final Deliverables.pptx"): lists Z.immerse alongside Home/PDP/PLP/Search/Wishlist/Store Locator and separately alongside Cart/Checkout/Order confirmation/My Account — appears to be a page-grouping list for deliverables scope, not an authoring-strategy statement.

No page anywhere proposes extending the Z.immerse/Experience-Builder pattern to footer, nav, homepage, PLP, or PDP.

## 3. Page 318472193 (Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations), read in full

This is an ops/environment runbook (environments, tokens, locales, scripts, setup checklist). It does **not** state a strategy for which content types use Experience Builder vs. coded components. Its only relevant content is operational:
- A table showing **current build state**: "Studio Experiences definitions" location (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts`) with **current types: CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage** — versus "Editorial content types" (`scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`) with **current type: shoppableImage**.
- *"Install Contentful Studio app in the space (required for Visual Editor / Experiences SDK)"* — setup step only.

No roadmap or scope statement here.

## 4. "Zimmermann - Enterprise Onboarding Kickoff.pdf" (attachment att346554371)

Searched multiple ways (title-scoped search, "Experience Builder" + title filter, generic strategy terms). This is a **generic Contentful vendor sales/kickoff deck** — title slide "Enterprise Onboarding Kickoff," "Your Onboarding Experts," a "Scope of Engagement" slide, and an "Authors & Editors" slide (appears to be a generic roles-definition slide, not Zimmermann-specific strategy). No text surfaced mentioning Experience Builder as an agreed primary authoring paradigm, or any Zimmermann-specific component-scope decision. This appears to be boilerplate Contentful onboarding collateral, not a strategy document.

## 5. Comments across Contentful-related pages for Tim Lavelle's statements

I confirmed the exact quotes from your context exist as **unresolved inline comments on page 346783750** (found via full-text comment search; oddly, `confluence_get_comments` on that page did not return these two, possibly a pagination/caching gap in the tool — but `confluence_search` located them directly):

- **Comment 379125773** (author attribution shows as directed at "Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz / Marcel Angelo Navarro"): *"I'm not sure we need to seperate these and the components we build will most of the time being used in an experience builder."*
- **Comment 379453460**: *"Authors will place elements on a page"*

I found **no reply** to either comment in the data returned (no Marcel/Jhoan response quoted or indexed), and **no other page or comment thread anywhere in the space** contains Tim Lavelle making a similar statement about component architecture or authoring strategy. All 24 *other* inline comments on 346783750 (retrieved via `confluence_get_comments`) are on unrelated topics (MRT apps TSD split, Sprint 1/2 content-type validation, PLP pagination spike, monitoring/New Relic, environment/Space decision) — none touch the Studio-vs-coded question.

## 6. Page 303071234 (04.1.1 Homepage and Content), read in full

Requirements are all "Confirmed" HPC items. The one arguably relevant line:
- **HPC-010**: *"The system should support reusable page builder templates across page types."*

This is the only requirements-level language suggesting reusable "page builder templates" apply "across page types" (not scoped to Z.immerse). However, it is ambiguous on its face — it does not name "Experience Builder," Contentful, or Studio, and could equally describe reusable coded page templates (e.g., shared Chakra layout templates for PDP/PLP/homepage), which is exactly what 04.2 Design Tracker and the PWA TSD describe elsewhere. I found nothing that resolves this ambiguity toward "Experience Builder specifically."

No other HPC requirement in this page assigns footer, nav, homepage modules, PLP, or PDP editorial slots to Experience Builder — the only content/CMS authoring requirements (HPC-001 through HPC-012) describe Contentful as sole CMS but never specify Experience Builder as the mechanism.

## 7. Discovery/kickoff strategy documents

- **att288849929 "Final Deliverables.pptx"**: only a page-grouping list (as above), not an authoring-model statement.
- No "Zimmermann Digital Modernisation" deck was found in the space by that name. **Page 269287425** (1.1 Purpose, Objectives, Scope & Success Criteria) is the closest strategic-kickoff document; it mentions *"A scalable, headless, composable, API-first architecture"* at a generic architectural-principles level, with no mention of Experience Builder, Studio, or component authoring split at all.

## Bottom line

The only two things in Confluence that speak to this question directly are: (1) the TSD's own stated rule in section 5.5 of page 346783750, which defaults to coded components and scopes Studio Experience narrowly to Z.immerse + campaign/marketing landing pages, and (2) Tim Lavelle's two unresolved inline comments (379125773, 379453460) on that same page pushing back on the separation. I found no other Confluence page, requirement, decision log, or attachment — including the Contentful vendor onboarding deck and the PWA TSD — that states or implies a broader strategic intent to use Experience Builder for footer, nav, homepage, PLP, or PDP. The disagreement appears to exist only in those two inline comments, with no reply or resolution recorded anywhere in the space.
