Real findings this time — and one of them directly contradicts something our TSD itself asserts. Here's what turned up.

## The concrete clue: Jira SFCC-51, and it exposes a mis-classification in our own §5.5

**SFCC-51 "Promotional Announcement Banner UI"** — Tim's comment (13363, 2026-07-07):
> "As this will be a component in the Contenful Studio builder, users can drag-n-drop where this lives on specific pages, but if this is going to live on a PLP and/or PDP or Global across all but Zimmerse, then will likely need a configuration to target specific SFCC Category IDs and Product IDs."

And it made it into the ticket's **accepted acceptance criteria** (comment 13387):
> "Given the promotional banner is placed on a PDP or PLP **via Contentful Studio**, when it is configured with one or more SFCC Category IDs and/or Product IDs, then the banner is only displayed when the shopper is viewing a matching category or product page."

Here's why this matters directly: **our TSD's §5.5 explicitly lists "announcement banner" as an example of a coded content-type component** — under "Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, **announcement banner**, size guide." But Tim's own prior, already-accepted decision on this exact component says it's placed via **Contentful Studio drag-and-drop** — i.e., a Studio Experience, not a coded fixed slot. We put a real example in the wrong bucket.

It also directly evidences comment #14. The mechanism Tim describes — "users can drag-n-drop where this lives on specific pages" — is literally an instance of our own heuristic's Studio-Experience trigger ("does the author decide placement and neighbours?"). So SFCC-51 isn't proof our heuristic is wrong in principle; it's proof we misapplied it to one of our own listed examples. That's consistent with #13 too: if a component we assumed was "fixed template slot" turns out to already be author-placed via Studio, Tim's "most of the time will end up in an experience builder" isn't an abstract preference — it's something that already happened on a real ticket.

## Corroborating, but not fully agreeing: an unmerged draft dev guide

`.docs/temp/humanContentfulGuide.md:126` (on branch `feature/contentfulDoc`, PR #38 "Draft Contentful developer guide," **still open**, author Hardi Sempuno, last touched 2026-07-17 — not signed off):
> "Pages that are fully content-managed (like the home page and campaign/collection pages) use Contentful Studio Experiences (the WYSIWYG). **The homepage is planned to be an Experience** ... While things like parts of the PLP, the footer, and **the announcement banner/bar are regular content entries** with editorial fields alongside their SFCC data."

This pushes the same direction as Tim (more things become Experience-driven than our TSD assumes) — it says the **homepage** is planned to become a Studio Experience, which also contradicts our §5.5 example list (which puts "homepage modules" in the coded bucket, matching how the homepage is actually built today via `useContentfulEntries`). But it **disagrees with SFCC-51 on the banner specifically** — this guide calls the banner a regular (coded) content entry, the opposite of what Tim decided on the ticket. So two independent sources both say "our TSD undercounts Studio Experience usage," but they don't agree on which components move.

## A weaker, ambiguous hint

Confluence page 303071234, **HPC-010**: *"The system should support reusable page builder templates across page types."* Could support Tim's direction (page builder = Experience Builder, applied broadly) — but it doesn't name Contentful, Studio, or Experience Builder at all, and could equally describe reusable coded Chakra templates. Flagged honestly as ambiguous, not resolving anything on its own.

## What's still not found anywhere

- **SFCC-10 (Z.immerse)** remains scoped exactly as before in every source checked — no epic, comment, or dependency suggests its pattern was meant to expand to footer/nav/homepage/PLP/PDP generally.
- **Footer, nav, PLP inserts, PDP tabs** — zero evidence in Jira or Confluence one way or the other. SFCC-55, 90, 94, 96 have comment threads, none touching Studio vs. coded.

- The four already-built coded components (`heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `productHero`, `videoEmbed`) have zero commits since their initial build — no migration signal in the code itself.

## Net assessment

This doesn't fully resolve 13/14, but it changes the picture materially: it's no longer just Tim's unsupported opinion against our validated rule. There's a real, already-accepted ticket (SFCC-51) where our own example classification was wrong, plus an independent draft source agreeing the trend runs the same direction (even if it disagrees on specifics). The honest scope of what's proven: **the banner example in §5.5 is misclassified and should move to Studio Experience** — that much has a direct citation. Whether footer, nav, homepage modules, PLP inserts, and PDP tabs also move is still genuinely unresolved by anything in Jira or Confluence — that part of comment #13 ("most of the time") still needs Tim's direct answer in the sync, since even his own two cited evidence points (SFCC-51 vs. the draft guide) don't agree with each other on which components beyond the banner move.

content.text:
Taking Tim's position at face value — Studio Experience as the default/primary path, not a narrow exception — the ripple goes well beyond §5.5. Here's everything it touches, split into what's now directly evidenced versus what becomes a new open question.

## 1. §5.5 itself — the rule and its rewrite

- **The rule's framing flips.** Currently: "coded by default; Studio Experience only for whole author-composed pages (Z.immerse/campaign)." Under Tim's position it becomes something like: "Studio Experience by default; coded only for [a narrower category still to be defined]."
- **The Heuristic bullet has to be replaced, not reworded.** "Does the author decide placement?" no longer discriminates anything if that's the norm (per #14) — a new criterion is needed, and neither Tim's comments nor the evidence we found state what it should be. This is a genuine gap, not a wording fix.
- **The example lists need correcting**, at minimum:
  - **"Announcement banner" moves out of the coded list** — SFCC-51's accepted AC directly contradicts its current classification.
  - **"Homepage modules" becomes uncertain** — the draft dev guide (`humanContentfulGuide.md`, unmerged) says homepage is "planned to be an Experience," which would also pull it out of the coded list, though this source isn't authoritative and conflicts with the same guide's own claim about the banner.
  - **Footer, nav, PLP inserts, PDP tabs** — no evidence either way. Under a literal "most of the time" reading they'd need to move too, but nothing found supports or rules that out.

## 2. §3/§4 Options Analysis — the bigger one

Option A's described mechanism (§3.2, §4.2) is a **coded-component + MRT-SSR-filter** model: entries fetched server-side, filtered by matching `sfccCategoryId`/`sfccProductId`, passed to a presentation-only React component. But SFCC-51's AC describes a **different** mechanism for the banner: the author places it via Contentful Studio drag-and-drop, and it's "configured with one or more SFCC Category IDs and/or Product IDs" — i.e., the ID-targeting is set as a property of the Studio placement itself, not resolved by an SSR filter against a coded content type's field.

If Studio Experience becomes the default for ID-targeted content, **Option A as written doesn't describe how most of these components would actually work.** This isn't a caveat-sized fix — it means either:
- Option A needs a second sub-mechanism documented (how SFCC-ID targeting works for a Studio-placed component instance, as opposed to a coded content-type field), or
- The whole options analysis gets re-scoped to cover both cases.

Either way, this is the section with the largest genuine rewrite, not just a relabeling.

## 3. §5.2 Component/API Changes

- The row adding `sfccCategoryId`/`sfccProductId` ShortText fields to content types shrinks in scope if fewer things are coded content types.
- The "one component per content type" row shifts emphasis toward the `experiences/` (Studio Experience) build path as the default location for new work, rather than `overrides/app/components/contentful/`.

## 4. §7 Risks — new items, and an entanglement with existing ones

- A new risk describing the dispute itself: the authoring-path rule is contested, SFCC-51 contradicts one of its own examples, and the scope beyond the banner is unresolved.
- A new, more consequential risk: **the mechanism for placing a Studio-authored, SFCC-ID-targeted component into an existing PWA-Kit commerce page (PDP/PLP) isn't proven anywhere in the codebase.** Today's `experiences/` + `/:slug` pattern composes a *whole page at a slug* — it doesn't inject a component into an existing dev-built PDP/PLP template. That's a different technical capability than what's built.
- That new risk **directly overlaps with two risks already in §7**: the uncarded "PLP grid-injection pagination/item-count" spike and the uncarded "PDP accordion mixed-content" spike. Both are already open questions about injecting external content into SFCC-rendered commerce pages without breaking existing behavior — if the injected content becomes Studio-placed rather than coded, those two spikes would need to investigate the Studio-injection mechanism specifically, not just a coded component's injection.

## 5. §8 Decision Record

The first decision row states the SSR-filter mechanism as the pattern, full stop. It would need to either fork into two decisions (one per mechanism) or be reframed as provisional pending which components actually go which path.

## 6. Appendices

- **Appendix A (Handoff Boundary):** the ownership split — "Composed pages (PDP/PLP editorial split) all pages outside Z.immerse [Accenture]" vs. "Z.immerse pages [Contentful squad]" — would need revisiting if editorial content *within* PDP/PLP (like the banner) becomes Studio-placed. Who registers that component, who configures its Studio placement, becomes ambiguous under the current two-row split.
- **Appendix C (Content Model Catalogue):** the Promotional Announcement Banner needs an explicit note that its mechanism is Studio Experience per SFCC-51, not silently folded into the generic Sprint-1 list. PLP Inline Grid Insert and PDP Accordion Content (both already flagged "uses sfccCategoryId/sfccProductId") would need their mechanism re-examined too, since if they follow the same pattern as the banner, their targeting isn't a coded content-type field being SSR-filtered — it's a Studio placement property.

## What this doesn't resolve, even if fully accepted

Taking Tim's position doesn't answer *how* Studio Experience placement + SFCC-ID targeting actually works technically — that mechanism isn't built or documented anywhere in the codebase today. Accepting his direction doesn't close that gap; it just means the gap needs investigating (likely overlapping with SFCC-238 and the two already-uncarded PLP/PDP spikes), which is new work, not a documentation change.

# SFCC Business Manager ↔ PWA Kit Region/Locale Sync — Findings & Implementation

## Context

Zimmermann's storefront config (which SFCC sites exist, what locales/currencies each
serves, what URL prefix each uses) originates in Salesforce Business Manager (BM) but has
to be manually re-created inside this PWA Kit repo for the storefront to route and render
each region correctly. This document started as investigation into how that sync worked
and where it was fragile, then became the design + implementation record once the SCAPI
sync option (formerly "Option A" below) was actually built out. **Status: implemented and
locally testing as of this update** — see "What's actually built" below. The known
7-vs-8-storefront count drift (US domestic/international split, per
`.docs/prd/regional.md` REG-005) is a separate, smaller fix and deliberately not detailed
here — it's easy and will be picked up on its own later.

## How sync worked before this PR — five hand-maintained locations, and this is Salesforce's documented pattern

BM config was manually transcribed into five locations (six files, two of which are
grouped pairs) that had to stay in lockstep: `.docs/prd/regional.md` (requirements source
of truth); `config/sites.js` + `config/default.js` together (the config PWA Kit actually
runs on — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (a second, independent config
keyed by URL slug — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (SFCC↔Contentful
mapping); and `e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` together (Playwright fixtures). See
"What's actually built" below for how this looks now — `sites.js`/`default.js` are joined
by `sites.generated.js`/`sites.overlay.js`, and `countries.ts`/`contentfulMapping.ts`/the
e2e fixtures each gained their own generated + overlay split too.

This is not a Zimmermann anti-pattern — Salesforce's own docs confirm `config/sites.js`
exists specifically to be manually kept in sync with Business Manager, and that
`l10n.supportedLocales` "must match" BM's locale settings, by design. Salesforce's newer
"Storefront Next" template consolidates this to one file (`config.server.ts`'s
`commerce.sites`) plus an env-var override, but even there `i18n.supportedLngs` still has
to be manually kept aligned with `commerce.sites[].supportedLocales` — the sync surface
shrinks, but a fully single-source-of-truth config doesn't exist anywhere Salesforce
documents, current or next-gen.

The one file that actually determines whether a region loads correctly at runtime is
`config/sites.js`: `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (`AppConfig.restore`)
resolves site+locale per request by scanning every site's `l10n.supportedLocales` for a
match against the URL's locale segment, and **falls back silently to the AU default site
if nothing matches — no error, no log**. Everything else (`countries.ts`,
`contentfulMapping.ts`, e2e fixtures) is a secondary mirror of whatever `sites.js` says.

## Option A — a SCAPI sync job to replace part of the manual transcription

OCAPI (the old Data API path for reading site config) is officially deprecated (April
2026, ~2-year patch-only tail). The relevant current SCAPI endpoint is confirmed:

- **`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/configurations?siteId={siteId}`**
  (`configuration/shopper-configurations/v1`, confirmed via
  `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s generated types — this is a real, typed client
  method already available in a dependency this repo has, not a new package).
- Returns a `siteConfiguration` entry covering **name, status, currencies, and locales**
  per site — exactly what `config/sites.js` needs to stay correct.
- **Uses the same SLAS shopper credentials already used elsewhere in this repo.** This is
  materially better than it first looked — the initially-found `sfcc.preferences`/`sfcc.sites`
  Admin APIs would have needed a brand-new Account Manager client_credentials setup;
  Shopper Configurations needs no new credential class at all.
- **One call per site — there's no org-wide "list all sites" call.** A sync script needs
  to already know the site ID list (which it does — it's the thing being verified).
- Explicitly documented as "highly cacheable" — this is designed for infrequent polling,
  not a per-request call. **Confirms the user's instinct: this should be a sync job run on
  demand or on a schedule (e.g. a `scripts/sfcc/` script analogous to
  `scripts/contentful/setup/detectDrift.mjs`, run manually before a release or on a cron),
  never called at runtime from the storefront itself.**

**What this closes, and what it doesn't:** a sync job here can _verify_ `config/sites.js`
against live BM (site status, locales, currencies) and flag drift — but it can't safely
_auto-write_ `config/sites.js`, since that file is Tier 1 and any write still needs
Integration-team review. Realistic shape: a `detect:regional-drift`-style script that
exits non-zero and prints a diff when BM and `config/sites.js` disagree, run manually or
in CI, not an auto-fix. This directly addresses the "5 files, easy to miss one" concern —
it wouldn't eliminate the files, but it would catch drift in the most important one
(`config/sites.js`) without hand-comparing against a BM screenshot.

**Update: built, and taken further than originally scoped here** — see "What's actually
built" below. Rather than a read-only drift-checker, the user (a verified
`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` member) opted to have the script actually write the
derived config, extended to all four hand-maintained files, not just `config/sites.js`.

### Could this go further than a drift-check — e.g. generate/override `sites.js` instead of just diffing it?

We checked whether Salesforce's newer "Storefront Next" template's approach (one config
file, overridable via a single env var, `PUBLIC__app__commerce__sites` — see
`zimmermann-sfn`'s `docs/README-CONFIG.md`) is portable here. **It is not, directly** —
that's a Vite-build-time mechanism specific to Storefront Next's SDK generation. The
current PWA Kit's config loader (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config.server.js`,
`getConfig()`) does whole-file selection only (`config/{tier}.js` → `config/default.js`
via `cosmiconfigSync`, keyed off `DEPLOY_TARGET`) — there is no env-var merge step
anywhere in it. A same-*spirit* mechanism could be hand-built from scratch (`config/sites.js`
is just a plain `module.exports`, so nothing stops it reading an env var or a generated
file itself) — but that would be new engineering inspired by sfn, not a port of anything,
and MRT's practical env-var size limits for a multi-KB JSON blob are unconfirmed.

More importantly, **even a generated/overridden `sites.js` would not eliminate the
hand-maintenance, only shrink part of it.** The Shopper Configurations response can supply
locale-ID and currency truth, but it has no concept of Zimmermann's `alias` field (the URL
prefix, e.g. `fr-eu`) or the `sfccSiteId` override (how the 4 fake EU sites point at one
real SFCC site) — both are pure PWA-Kit/Zimmermann routing concepts that don't exist in
Business Manager or SCAPI at all. So the realistic ceiling is a **hybrid**: SCAPI-sourced
locale/currency data plus a permanently hand-maintained small overlay for routing/alias
data — and a script that *writes* any part of `config/sites.js` (even generated) is a
bigger governance ask than the read-only drift-checker above, needing explicit
Integration-team design sign-off before any code is written, not just implementation
approval.

**Honest framing:** this makes locale/currency drift *catchable, and eventually
automatable*. It does not make `config/sites.js` *not-hand-maintained* — URL routing config
stays manual permanently, because it structurally isn't a Business Manager/SCAPI concept
to sync from. Recommend treating "drift-check script" (read-only) and "generated overlay"
(writes, needs sign-off) as two separate, sequential asks — not one.

**Side finding, unrelated to this plan:** `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` is present
in this repo's `package.json`/`node_modules` even though nothing here uses it (this repo
runs `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`/`pwa-kit-runtime` v3.18.0, a different SDK generation
entirely). Worth understanding why it's there before it causes confusion later — out of
scope for this document.

## What's actually built

The "generate + hand-maintained overlay" pattern was extended to **all four** files, not
just `config/sites.js` — the user's explicit call was that BM changes should flow to every
consuming file when the sync script runs, not just the highest-leverage one.

### Files

| Kind | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Script | `scripts/sfcc/_shared.mjs`, `scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs` | `npm run sync:regional-config` (`-- --dry-run` for a no-write preview) |
| Generated (rewritten every sync) | `config/sites.generated.js` | per real SFCC site: status/defaultLocale/defaultCurrency/supportedCurrencies/supportedLocales |
| Generated | `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` | per URL slug: sfccSiteId/locale/currency |
| Generated | `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts` | SUPPORTED_LOCALES + SITE_LOCALES per PWA site id |
| Generated | `e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js` | per e2e fixture key: locale/currency/currencySymbol/siteId — self-contained, no merge needed downstream |
| Hand-maintained overlay | `config/sites.overlay.js` | id/sfccSiteId/locale-id/alias per PWA site (10 entries) |
| Hand-maintained overlay | `e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js` | fixture key → PWA site id (10 entries) |
| Hand-maintained overlay | inline in `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` | shippingCountry/checkoutOwner/globalEPricing/boutiqueRegion per slug — not a separate file, since `countries.ts` isn't on the Hard-Rule-4 absolute list and could just be edited directly |
| Consumer (thin merge — written once by hand, **not** touched by `npm run sync:regional-config`) | `config/sites.js`, `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `e2e/fixtures/site.js` | Imports the generated + overlay files at load time; only needs a manual edit again if the merge *logic* itself changes, not when BM data changes |

### What the live API actually looks like (worth preserving — nothing in Salesforce's docs states this)

The Shopper Configurations response is **not** the nested object the SDK's `any`-typed
field suggests. It's a flat array of `{configurationType, id, value}` entries — one per
field — mixing `siteConfiguration` entries (`id`/`name`/`status`/`timezone`/
`defaultCurrency`/`allowedCurrencies`/`defaultLocale`/`allowedLocales`) with unrelated
`globalConfiguration` entries (`SalesforcePaymentsAllowed`, `my_domain`). Field names differ
from every guess made before seeing a real response: `allowedCurrencies` not `currencies`,
`allowedLocales` not `locales`. `allowedLocales` entries are rich objects
(`{id, country, displayName, ...}`) with **no per-locale currency field** and always
include a placeholder `{id: 'default', ...}` entry that isn't real. Since every site here
uses one currency across all its locales, each real locale is assigned the site's own
`defaultCurrency` rather than a (non-existent) per-locale value.

### Auth gotcha (also undocumented, cost real debugging time)

The guest `client_credentials` token request fails with `400 "Guest token requires a
channel_id parameter"` unless a `channel_id` (the SFCC site ID) is included in the token
request body — and a token is scoped to exactly one site, so the script requests a fresh
token per site rather than one shared token. Separately, an `401 "incorrect client type"`
error meant the existing SLAS client (used for the storefront's normal shopper login) had
no `sfcc.shopper-configurations` scope enabled — added via the SLAS Admin UI at
`https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/shopper/auth-admin/v1/ui/` (not a
generic Account Manager screen). Watch for the near-identical, wrong scope name
`sfcc.shopper-configuations` (missing an 'r') if this ever needs re-deriving from a search.

### Formatting

`JSON.stringify`'s output (double quotes, no trailing commas) fails this repo's
`prettier/prettier` eslint rule — the script runs `npx eslint --fix` on each file it writes
rather than hand-rolling a formatter that duplicates `.prettierrc`.

### Bug found and fixed along the way

`e2e/fixtures/customers.js`'s `ADDRESSES` map only had a single `eu` key and was missing
`euIntl` entirely — pre-existing, unrelated to this work, but became a live mismatch once
`site.js` gained the correct 4-way EU split (`enEu`/`frEu`/`itEu`/`esEu`) plus `euIntl`.
Fixed with per-locale addresses (Berlin/Paris/Rome/Madrid/Zurich) so all 10 keys line up
across both files.

### Verification run (2026-07-17)

`node --check` on every new/changed `.js`/`.mjs`, a functional `require()` smoke test of
`e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` + `config/sites.js`, `npx eslint` (clean) and
`npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) across every touched file. Followed by a local `npm start` pass
hitting all ten regional URLs and confirming each resolved the expected site/locale
(root `/` → AU/`en`, `/us/` → US/`en-US`, `/uk/` → UK/`en-GB`, `/en-eu/` `/fr-eu/` `/it-eu/`
`/es-eu/` → the four EU locales, `/en-ch/` → EU Intl/`en-CH`, `/hk/` → HK/`en-HK`,
`/en-ae/` → ME/`en-AE`) — this is what caught the `defaultLocale` bug documented below.

### Known current-state quirk (expected, not a bug)

The dev realm's live data currently returns `HK: USD` and `ME: EUR`, not the documented
production targets `HKD`/`AED` — almost certainly this dev sandbox not being fully
configured with production currencies yet. This is exactly the kind of drift this pipeline
now surfaces automatically; once BM is corrected, re-running `npm run sync:regional-config`
will pull the right values into all four generated files in one pass.

### Real bug found in local testing (fixed)

`config/sites.js`'s merge logic originally set `l10n.defaultLocale: source.defaultLocale`
— SCAPI's **site-level** default for the real SFCC site, not scoped to the one locale a
given PWA site actually supports. This crashed `npm start` immediately: BM's
`ZimmermannAU` default is `en-AU`, but the `ZimmermannAU` PWA site's overlay only lists
`en` — so `defaultLocale` pointed at a locale absent from `supportedLocales`,
`_app-config`'s `AppConfig.restore` failed both locale lookups, and crashed on
`undefined.alias`. Same bug would have hit `ZimmermannEUfr`/`EUit`/`EUes` too (BM's shared
`ZimmermannEU` default `en-GB` only matches `EUen`). **Fix:** `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`
instead — every PWA site has exactly one locale in its overlay by design, so that locale
*is* its default; SCAPI's notion of "default" belongs to the real SFCC site, not to
Zimmermann's per-locale PWA site split, and should never have been used here.

### Open item carried over from the original US-split design

`countries.ts`'s hand-maintained overlay still has an `en-ca` (US international) entry
defined, but it's excluded from the live `COUNTRIES` export by construction — there's no
matching entry in `config/sites.overlay.js` yet, since `ZimmermannUSIntl`'s real site ID is
still unconfirmed in BM (see "Where this leaves the earlier US-split remediation" below,
unchanged).

## Option B — consolidate the EU 4-way site split (separate from the above, no framework migration needed)

Zimmermann currently models EU domestic as **4 fake PWA sites**
(`ZimmermannEUen`/`fr`/`it`/`es`), each with one locale, all sharing one real
`sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'`. We asked whether this split is actually required by the
current PWA Kit SDK, or self-imposed. **Confirmed self-imposed, not required** —
Salesforce's own shipped reference config (`RefArchGlobal` in the upstream `pwa-kit` repo)
has a single site with **16 locales** in one `supportedLocales` array. The underlying SDK
functions (`getConfigMatcher`, `getLocaleByReference`, `resolveLocaleFromUrl` in
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/site-utils.js`) all operate generically
over locale arrays of any length — there's no 1-locale-per-site limitation in the SDK
itself.

**But this is not a trivial merge, and it interacts with other things in this document —
read before acting on either:**

- **The comment in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`** explaining why the
  custom resolution hack exists ("because `url.site` is `'none'`...") **is factually wrong
  for the current config** — `config/default.js` actually sets `url.site: 'path'`. This is
  a small, separate doc/comment cleanup, unrelated to whether consolidation happens.
- **The custom `_app-config` override should be kept, not removed, if consolidating** — it
  currently produces the same result as the stock SDK function for the 4-fake-site model
  (effectively redundant today), but a live empirical test found the stock SDK's
  locale-matching regex has a real prefix-collision bug (`fr` matches before `fr-eu` in its
  alternation list, truncating the match) that the _consolidated_ single-site model would
  hit — and the custom hack's `id`-or-`alias` matching happens to already tolerate it.
  Removing the hack while consolidating would break `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`.
- **Outbound URL generation needs rework, not just config.** `createUrlTemplate` decides
  the URL's site-vs-locale segment from `site.alias`; a consolidated site has no per-locale
  alias, so URLs would need to be generated from the locale segment instead — a real
  logic change in how `locals.buildUrl` is constructed, not a `sites.js`-only edit.
- **This conflict is now resolved in favor of the 4-site model — reversing it is the cost
  of pursuing Option B.** `e2e/fixtures/site.js` (and its generation pipeline, and
  `e2e/fixtures/customers.js`) now use the 4-key split (`enEu`/`frEu`/`itEu`/`esEu`) plus
  `euIntl`, matching today's `config/sites.js`. If EU consolidation happens later, all of
  `e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js`, the sync script's e2e-derivation logic, and
  `customers.js`'s `ADDRESSES` map would need to collapse back to a single `eu` key —
  budget for that alongside the URL-generation rework below.
- `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` needs **no structural change** either way — it's
  already keyed by URL slug with `sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'` on every EU entry (now via
  `countries.generated.ts`, but the shape is the same), effectively pre-consolidated.
- `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` would collapse
  from 4 keys to 1 (`ZimmermannEU: ['en-GB','fr','it','es']`) if consolidating — this is
  now script-derived rather than hand-written, so the change would happen automatically on
  the next sync once `config/sites.overlay.js` is consolidated, not as a separate manual
  edit.

**Net effect if pursued:** `config/sites.js`'s EU block goes from 4 objects to 1 (one
fewer thing to keep in sync across the 5-file chain for EU specifically), but the
resolution/URL-generation code doesn't get simpler — it stays and does real work. This is
worth doing for config-sync hygiene, but it's a scoped piece of engineering work with
real behavioural risk (URL generation, a regex edge case), not a free cleanup.

## Where this leaves the earlier US-split remediation

Still pending BM confirming `ZimmermannUSIntl`'s real site ID and locale ID — unaffected by
either the sync pipeline or the EU-consolidation question. Slightly easier now than
originally drafted: adding the new site to `config/sites.overlay.js` and its overlay entry
in `countries.ts` no longer needs a direct edit to the absolute-blocked `config/sites.js`
(that file is now just merge logic, regenerated automatically). **`config/default.js`'s
`siteAliases` map still needs a manual entry (`ZimmermannUSIntl: 'en-ca'`) and remains
absolutely off-limits regardless of approver status** — that one edit still has to be made
by hand, by a human, per `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule #4.

## Status

- **Option A (SCAPI sync pipeline): implemented**, extended to all four files per the
  user's decision, currently in local testing. See "What's actually built" above.
- **Option B (EU 4-way consolidation): still undecided, not implemented.** Worth doing for
  config-sync hygiene, but real behavioural risk (URL generation, a regex edge case) and
  now a wider blast radius than originally scoped — it also touches the e2e fixture
  generation pipeline built for Option A, not just `config/sites.js` and `countries.ts`.

# SFCC Business Manager ↔ PWA Kit Region/Locale Sync — Findings & Implementation

## Context

Zimmermann's storefront config (which SFCC sites exist, what locales/currencies each
serves, what URL prefix each uses) originates in Salesforce Business Manager (BM) but has
to be manually re-created inside this PWA Kit repo for the storefront to route and render
each region correctly. This document started as investigation into how that sync worked
and where it was fragile, then became the design + implementation record once the SCAPI
sync option (formerly "Option A" below) was actually built out. **Status: implemented and
locally testing as of this update** — see "What's actually built" below. The known
7-vs-8-storefront count drift (US domestic/international split, per
`.docs/prd/regional.md` REG-005) is a separate, smaller fix and deliberately not detailed
here — it's easy and will be picked up on its own later.

## How sync worked before this PR — five hand-maintained locations, and this is Salesforce's documented pattern

BM config was manually transcribed into five locations (six files, two of which are
grouped pairs) that had to stay in lockstep: `.docs/prd/regional.md` (requirements source
of truth); `config/sites.js` + `config/default.js` together (the config PWA Kit actually
runs on — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (a second, independent config
keyed by URL slug — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (SFCC↔Contentful
mapping); and `e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` together (Playwright fixtures). See
"What's actually built" below for how this looks now — `sites.js`/`default.js` are joined
by `sites.generated.js`/`sites.overlay.js`, and `countries.ts`/`contentfulMapping.ts`/the
e2e fixtures each gained their own generated + overlay split too.

This is not a Zimmermann anti-pattern — Salesforce's own docs confirm `config/sites.js`
exists specifically to be manually kept in sync with Business Manager, and that
`l10n.supportedLocales` "must match" BM's locale settings, by design. Salesforce's newer
"Storefront Next" template consolidates this to one file (`config.server.ts`'s
`commerce.sites`) plus an env-var override, but even there `i18n.supportedLngs` still has
to be manually kept aligned with `commerce.sites[].supportedLocales` — the sync surface
shrinks, but a fully single-source-of-truth config doesn't exist anywhere Salesforce
documents, current or next-gen.

The one file that actually determines whether a region loads correctly at runtime is
`config/sites.js`: `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (`AppConfig.restore`)
resolves site+locale per request by scanning every site's `l10n.supportedLocales` for a
match against the URL's locale segment, and **falls back silently to the AU default site
if nothing matches — no error, no log**. Everything else (`countries.ts`,
`contentfulMapping.ts`, e2e fixtures) is a secondary mirror of whatever `sites.js` says.

## Option A — a SCAPI sync job to replace part of the manual transcription

OCAPI (the old Data API path for reading site config) is officially deprecated (April
2026, ~2-year patch-only tail). The relevant current SCAPI endpoint is confirmed:

- **`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/configurations?siteId={siteId}`**
  (`configuration/shopper-configurations/v1`, confirmed via
  `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s generated types — this is a real, typed client
  method already available in a dependency this repo has, not a new package).
- Returns a `siteConfiguration` entry covering **name, status, currencies, and locales**
  per site — exactly what `config/sites.js` needs to stay correct.
- **Uses the same SLAS shopper credentials already used elsewhere in this repo.** This is
  materially better than it first looked — the initially-found `sfcc.preferences`/`sfcc.sites`
  Admin APIs would have needed a brand-new Account Manager client_credentials setup;
  Shopper Configurations needs no new credential class at all.
- **One call per site — there's no org-wide "list all sites" call.** A sync script needs
  to already know the site ID list (which it does — it's the thing being verified).
- Explicitly documented as "highly cacheable" — this is designed for infrequent polling,
  not a per-request call. **Confirms the user's instinct: this should be a sync job run on
  demand or on a schedule (e.g. a `scripts/sfcc/` script analogous to
  `scripts/contentful/setup/detectDrift.mjs`, run manually before a release or on a cron),
  never called at runtime from the storefront itself.**

**What this closes, and what it doesn't:** a sync job here can _verify_ `config/sites.js`
against live BM (site status, locales, currencies) and flag drift — but it can't safely
_auto-write_ `config/sites.js`, since that file is Tier 1 and any write still needs
Integration-team review. Realistic shape: a `detect:regional-drift`-style script that
exits non-zero and prints a diff when BM and `config/sites.js` disagree, run manually or
in CI, not an auto-fix. This directly addresses the "5 files, easy to miss one" concern —
it wouldn't eliminate the files, but it would catch drift in the most important one
(`config/sites.js`) without hand-comparing against a BM screenshot.

**Update: built, and taken further than originally scoped here** — see "What's actually
built" below. Rather than a read-only drift-checker, the user (a verified
`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` member) opted to have the script actually write the
derived config, extended to all four hand-maintained files, not just `config/sites.js`.

### Could this go further than a drift-check — e.g. generate/override `sites.js` instead of just diffing it?

We checked whether Salesforce's newer "Storefront Next" template's approach (one config
file, overridable via a single env var, `PUBLIC__app__commerce__sites` — see
`zimmermann-sfn`'s `docs/README-CONFIG.md`) is portable here. **It is not, directly** —
that's a Vite-build-time mechanism specific to Storefront Next's SDK generation. The
current PWA Kit's config loader (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config.server.js`,
`getConfig()`) does whole-file selection only (`config/{tier}.js` → `config/default.js`
via `cosmiconfigSync`, keyed off `DEPLOY_TARGET`) — there is no env-var merge step
anywhere in it. A same-*spirit* mechanism could be hand-built from scratch (`config/sites.js`
is just a plain `module.exports`, so nothing stops it reading an env var or a generated
file itself) — but that would be new engineering inspired by sfn, not a port of anything,
and MRT's practical env-var size limits for a multi-KB JSON blob are unconfirmed.

More importantly, **even a generated/overridden `sites.js` would not eliminate the
hand-maintenance, only shrink part of it.** The Shopper Configurations response can supply
locale-ID and currency truth, but it has no concept of Zimmermann's `alias` field (the URL
prefix, e.g. `fr-eu`) or the `sfccSiteId` override (how the 4 fake EU sites point at one
real SFCC site) — both are pure PWA-Kit/Zimmermann routing concepts that don't exist in
Business Manager or SCAPI at all. So the realistic ceiling is a **hybrid**: SCAPI-sourced
locale/currency data plus a permanently hand-maintained small overlay for routing/alias
data — and a script that *writes* any part of `config/sites.js` (even generated) is a
bigger governance ask than the read-only drift-checker above, needing explicit
Integration-team design sign-off before any code is written, not just implementation
approval.

**Honest framing:** this makes locale/currency drift *catchable, and eventually
automatable*. It does not make `config/sites.js` *not-hand-maintained* — URL routing config
stays manual permanently, because it structurally isn't a Business Manager/SCAPI concept
to sync from. Recommend treating "drift-check script" (read-only) and "generated overlay"
(writes, needs sign-off) as two separate, sequential asks — not one.

**Side finding, unrelated to this plan:** `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` is present
in this repo's `package.json`/`node_modules` even though nothing here uses it (this repo
runs `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`/`pwa-kit-runtime` v3.18.0, a different SDK generation
entirely). Worth understanding why it's there before it causes confusion later — out of
scope for this document.

## What's actually built

The "generate + hand-maintained overlay" pattern was extended to **all four** files, not
just `config/sites.js` — the user's explicit call was that BM changes should flow to every
consuming file when the sync script runs, not just the highest-leverage one.

### Files

| Kind | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Script | `scripts/sfcc/_shared.mjs`, `scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs` | `npm run sync:regional-config` (`-- --dry-run` for a no-write preview) |
| Generated (rewritten every sync) | `config/sites.generated.js` | per real SFCC site: status/defaultLocale/defaultCurrency/supportedCurrencies/supportedLocales |
| Generated | `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` | per URL slug: sfccSiteId/locale/currency |
| Generated | `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts` | SUPPORTED_LOCALES + SITE_LOCALES per PWA site id |
| Generated | `e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js` | per e2e fixture key: locale/currency/currencySymbol/siteId — self-contained, no merge needed downstream |
| Hand-maintained overlay | `config/sites.overlay.js` | id/sfccSiteId/locale-id/alias per PWA site (10 entries) |
| Hand-maintained overlay | `e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js` | fixture key → PWA site id (10 entries) |
| Hand-maintained overlay | inline in `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` | shippingCountry/checkoutOwner/globalEPricing/boutiqueRegion per slug — not a separate file, since `countries.ts` isn't on the Hard-Rule-4 absolute list and could just be edited directly |
| Consumer (thin merge — written once by hand, **not** touched by `npm run sync:regional-config`) | `config/sites.js`, `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `e2e/fixtures/site.js` | Imports the generated + overlay files at load time; only needs a manual edit again if the merge *logic* itself changes, not when BM data changes |

### What the live API actually looks like (worth preserving — nothing in Salesforce's docs states this)

The Shopper Configurations response is **not** the nested object the SDK's `any`-typed
field suggests. It's a flat array of `{configurationType, id, value}` entries — one per
field — mixing `siteConfiguration` entries (`id`/`name`/`status`/`timezone`/
`defaultCurrency`/`allowedCurrencies`/`defaultLocale`/`allowedLocales`) with unrelated
`globalConfiguration` entries (`SalesforcePaymentsAllowed`, `my_domain`). Field names differ
from every guess made before seeing a real response: `allowedCurrencies` not `currencies`,
`allowedLocales` not `locales`. `allowedLocales` entries are rich objects
(`{id, country, displayName, ...}`) with **no per-locale currency field** and always
include a placeholder `{id: 'default', ...}` entry that isn't real. Since every site here
uses one currency across all its locales, each real locale is assigned the site's own
`defaultCurrency` rather than a (non-existent) per-locale value.

### Auth gotcha (also undocumented, cost real debugging time)

The guest `client_credentials` token request fails with `400 "Guest token requires a
channel_id parameter"` unless a `channel_id` (the SFCC site ID) is included in the token
request body — and a token is scoped to exactly one site, so the script requests a fresh
token per site rather than one shared token. Separately, an `401 "incorrect client type"`
error meant the existing SLAS client (used for the storefront's normal shopper login) had
no `sfcc.shopper-configurations` scope enabled — added via the SLAS Admin UI at
`https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/shopper/auth-admin/v1/ui/` (not a
generic Account Manager screen). Watch for the near-identical, wrong scope name
`sfcc.shopper-configuations` (missing an 'r') if this ever needs re-deriving from a search.

### Formatting

`JSON.stringify`'s output (double quotes, no trailing commas) fails this repo's
`prettier/prettier` eslint rule — the script runs `npx eslint --fix` on each file it writes
rather than hand-rolling a formatter that duplicates `.prettierrc`.

### Bug found and fixed along the way

`e2e/fixtures/customers.js`'s `ADDRESSES` map only had a single `eu` key and was missing
`euIntl` entirely — pre-existing, unrelated to this work, but became a live mismatch once
`site.js` gained the correct 4-way EU split (`enEu`/`frEu`/`itEu`/`esEu`) plus `euIntl`.
Fixed with per-locale addresses (Berlin/Paris/Rome/Madrid/Zurich) so all 10 keys line up
across both files.

### Verification run (2026-07-17)

`node --check` on every new/changed `.js`/`.mjs`, a functional `require()` smoke test of
`e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` + `config/sites.js`, `npx eslint` (clean) and
`npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) across every touched file. Followed by a local `npm start` pass
hitting all ten regional URLs and confirming each resolved the expected site/locale
(root `/` → AU/`en`, `/us/` → US/`en-US`, `/uk/` → UK/`en-GB`, `/en-eu/` `/fr-eu/` `/it-eu/`
`/es-eu/` → the four EU locales, `/en-ch/` → EU Intl/`en-CH`, `/hk/` → HK/`en-HK`,
`/en-ae/` → ME/`en-AE`) — this is what caught the `defaultLocale` bug documented below.

### Known current-state quirk (expected, not a bug)

The dev realm's live data currently returns `HK: USD` and `ME: EUR`, not the documented
production targets `HKD`/`AED` — almost certainly this dev sandbox not being fully
configured with production currencies yet. This is exactly the kind of drift this pipeline
now surfaces automatically; once BM is corrected, re-running `npm run sync:regional-config`
will pull the right values into all four generated files in one pass.

### Real bug found in local testing (fixed)

`config/sites.js`'s merge logic originally set `l10n.defaultLocale: source.defaultLocale`
— SCAPI's **site-level** default for the real SFCC site, not scoped to the one locale a
given PWA site actually supports. This crashed `npm start` immediately: BM's
`ZimmermannAU` default is `en-AU`, but the `ZimmermannAU` PWA site's overlay only lists
`en` — so `defaultLocale` pointed at a locale absent from `supportedLocales`,
`_app-config`'s `AppConfig.restore` failed both locale lookups, and crashed on
`undefined.alias`. Same bug would have hit `ZimmermannEUfr`/`EUit`/`EUes` too (BM's shared
`ZimmermannEU` default `en-GB` only matches `EUen`). **Fix:** `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`
instead — every PWA site has exactly one locale in its overlay by design, so that locale
*is* its default; SCAPI's notion of "default" belongs to the real SFCC site, not to
Zimmermann's per-locale PWA site split, and should never have been used here.

### Open item carried over from the original US-split design

`countries.ts`'s hand-maintained overlay still has an `en-ca` (US international) entry
defined, but it's excluded from the live `COUNTRIES` export by construction — there's no
matching entry in `config/sites.overlay.js` yet, since `ZimmermannUSIntl`'s real site ID is
still unconfirmed in BM (see "Where this leaves the earlier US-split remediation" below,
unchanged).

## Option B — consolidate the EU 4-way site split (separate from the above, no framework migration needed)

Zimmermann currently models EU domestic as **4 fake PWA sites**
(`ZimmermannEUen`/`fr`/`it`/`es`), each with one locale, all sharing one real
`sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'`. We asked whether this split is actually required by the
current PWA Kit SDK, or self-imposed. **Confirmed self-imposed, not required** —
Salesforce's own shipped reference config (`RefArchGlobal` in the upstream `pwa-kit` repo)
has a single site with **16 locales** in one `supportedLocales` array. The underlying SDK
functions (`getConfigMatcher`, `getLocaleByReference`, `resolveLocaleFromUrl` in
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/site-utils.js`) all operate generically
over locale arrays of any length — there's no 1-locale-per-site limitation in the SDK
itself.

**But this is not a trivial merge, and it interacts with other things in this document —
read before acting on either:**

- **The comment in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`** explaining why the
  custom resolution hack exists ("because `url.site` is `'none'`...") **is factually wrong
  for the current config** — `config/default.js` actually sets `url.site: 'path'`. This is
  a small, separate doc/comment cleanup, unrelated to whether consolidation happens.
- **The custom `_app-config` override should be kept, not removed, if consolidating** — it
  currently produces the same result as the stock SDK function for the 4-fake-site model
  (effectively redundant today), but a live empirical test found the stock SDK's
  locale-matching regex has a real prefix-collision bug (`fr` matches before `fr-eu` in its
  alternation list, truncating the match) that the _consolidated_ single-site model would
  hit — and the custom hack's `id`-or-`alias` matching happens to already tolerate it.
  Removing the hack while consolidating would break `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`.
- **Outbound URL generation needs rework, not just config.** `createUrlTemplate` decides
  the URL's site-vs-locale segment from `site.alias`; a consolidated site has no per-locale
  alias, so URLs would need to be generated from the locale segment instead — a real
  logic change in how `locals.buildUrl` is constructed, not a `sites.js`-only edit.
- **This conflict is now resolved in favor of the 4-site model — reversing it is the cost
  of pursuing Option B.** `e2e/fixtures/site.js` (and its generation pipeline, and
  `e2e/fixtures/customers.js`) now use the 4-key split (`enEu`/`frEu`/`itEu`/`esEu`) plus
  `euIntl`, matching today's `config/sites.js`. If EU consolidation happens later, all of
  `e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js`, the sync script's e2e-derivation logic, and
  `customers.js`'s `ADDRESSES` map would need to collapse back to a single `eu` key —
  budget for that alongside the URL-generation rework below.
- `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` needs **no structural change** either way — it's
  already keyed by URL slug with `sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'` on every EU entry (now via
  `countries.generated.ts`, but the shape is the same), effectively pre-consolidated.
- `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` would collapse
  from 4 keys to 1 (`ZimmermannEU: ['en-GB','fr','it','es']`) if consolidating — this is
  now script-derived rather than hand-written, so the change would happen automatically on
  the next sync once `config/sites.overlay.js` is consolidated, not as a separate manual
  edit.

**Net effect if pursued:** `config/sites.js`'s EU block goes from 4 objects to 1 (one
fewer thing to keep in sync across the 5-file chain for EU specifically), but the
resolution/URL-generation code doesn't get simpler — it stays and does real work. This is
worth doing for config-sync hygiene, but it's a scoped piece of engineering work with
real behavioural risk (URL generation, a regex edge case), not a free cleanup.

## Where this leaves the earlier US-split remediation

Still pending BM confirming `ZimmermannUSIntl`'s real site ID and locale ID — unaffected by
either the sync pipeline or the EU-consolidation question. Slightly easier now than
originally drafted: adding the new site to `config/sites.overlay.js` and its overlay entry
in `countries.ts` no longer needs a direct edit to the absolute-blocked `config/sites.js`
(that file is now just merge logic, regenerated automatically). **`config/default.js`'s
`siteAliases` map still needs a manual entry (`ZimmermannUSIntl: 'en-ca'`) and remains
absolutely off-limits regardless of approver status** — that one edit still has to be made
by hand, by a human, per `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule #4.

## Status

- **Option A (SCAPI sync pipeline): implemented**, extended to all four files per the
  user's decision, currently in local testing. See "What's actually built" above.
- **Option B (EU 4-way consolidation): still undecided, not implemented.** Worth doing for
  config-sync hygiene, but real behavioural risk (URL generation, a regex edge case) and
  now a wider blast radius than originally scoped — it also touches the e2e fixture
  generation pipeline built for Option A, not just `config/sites.js` and `countries.ts`.

## What's confirmed (safe to cite to Tim)

**`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`** has a `COUNTRY_OVERLAY['en-ca']` entry, on disk, right now:
```
'en-ca': { shippingCountry: 'CA', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, // TBC — pending ZimmermannUSIntl
```
It's explicitly excluded from the live `COUNTRIES` export because there's no matching entry yet in the generated config — the file's own comment says so: *"'en-ca' (US international) is defined here ready to go, but has no matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet... until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added to config/sites.overlay.js (pending BM confirmation of the real site ID)."*

There's a dedicated planning doc, `.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md` (22 Jul 2026), that names this exact item directly: *"The known 7-vs-8-storefront count drift (US domestic/international split, per REG-005) is a separate, smaller fix and deliberately not detailed here — it's easy and will be picked up on its own later."* And later: *"Still pending BM confirming ZimmermannUSIntl's real site ID and locale ID."* This is a genuinely known, named, tracked item — not something we invented for the TSD. It also confirms the URL slug is settled (`config/default.js`'s `siteAliases` map will need `ZimmermannUSIntl: 'en-ca'`), and that shipping country (CA), Global-e checkout, and USD currency are already decided (README.md:169: *"United States | /us/ (domestic) · /en-ca/ (international) | USD | SFCC domestic · Global-e international"*).

So: **US-International = the US storefront's Canada-shipping variant, checked out via Global-e, still priced in USD** — a common DTC pattern where a US brand sells to Canada through Global-e as merchant-of-record for duties/tax/currency display, without a separate catalog or currency.

## What's genuinely NOT decided — and this is the actual answer to "what is the 10th locale"

**Nobody has decided the locale code yet.** The planning doc says the site ID *and* locale ID are both "pending BM confirming." This isn't us being vague — it's the honest state of a real open item.

If you want a defensible best-guess to offer Tim (clearly labeled as inference, not fact): every other Global-e-owned site that isn't sharing an SFCC site with domestic English content — `en-CH` (EU-International), `en-HK`, `en-AE` — got its own distinct locale matching its slug. The `en-eu` case is the *only* exception, because it's SFCC-owned checkout sharing the same SFCC site as three other EU sub-sites (so it reuses `en-GB` rather than getting its own locale). `en-ca`'s overlay entry matches the Global-e-owned pattern (`checkoutOwner: 'global-e'`, `globalEPricing: true`), not the `en-eu` pattern — so by precedent, **`en-CA` is the more likely outcome**, but that's pattern-matching against three prior cases, not a stated decision anywhere.

I initially found `"locale_text.message.en-CA": { "defaultMessage": "English (Canada)" }` in the translation files and thought it was confirming evidence. It isn't. 1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.

### 1.2 Problem

Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.
2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.
3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined.
4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners.
5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy.

*These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.*

---

2. Constraints & Assumptions
----------------------------

### 2.1 Constraints

| Constraint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. |
| Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |
| Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). |
| Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. |
| Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. |
| Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. |

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) |
| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |
| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.

#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)

Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.

#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*

Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.

---

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**

### 4.2 Rationale

Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.
* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).

---

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)

1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).
2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).
3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.
4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.
5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).
6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).
7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.

> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.

### 5.2 Component / API Changes

| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |
| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |
| `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified |
| `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified |
| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |

> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.

### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces

**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):

| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |
| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |
| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):

`{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: [],
}`

**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**

`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({
content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',
locale: currentLocale,
});
const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {
const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;
// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render
return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;
});
// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component
return matchedInserts;`

**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.

**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.

### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |
| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |
| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case |

> **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7.

### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes

**Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7.

**Token boundary.**

| Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Build-time only; never in MRT/bundle. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). |

**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:

* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.
* **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.
* **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.
* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.

---

6. Testing & Validation
-----------------------

### 6.1 Test Coverage

This spike produces findings and a design, not a testable build; the tests below belong to the downstream build stories.

| Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validation of findings (this spike) | The design cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence (maps to Section 1.4). | Every design claim traces to a verified source; current-versus-target state is stated honestly. |
| Unit (downstream) | SSR-side SFCC-ID filter; presentation-only component renders pre-filtered entries and null-returns on empty. | Filter selects matching + null-ID entries only; component holds no ID logic. |
| Integration (downstream) | SSR cache key includes the SFCC ID; publish webhook purges the correct keys. | No cross-page editorial bleed; content updates appear after publish within the SWR window. |
| E2E / Playwright (downstream) | Editorial content renders on the scoped category/product page and not elsewhere. | Observable in the UI across representative storefronts. |

### 6.2 Regression Risk

Low today: the reformatted design does not change running code. The material regression surface arrives with the downstream build, concentrated on two points that the build stories must cover explicitly: **SSR ID-filter correctness** and **cache-key isolation** (a wrong or missing key leaks editorial content across pages).

--------

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content, banners, size guides, promotional content, and global assets. Integration is via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA) for all customer-facing pages, with the Contentful Preview API (CPA) available server-side only.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | [DEV](https://app.contentful.com/spaces/u9kb6gp6slxu/environments/dev/) | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
