| 4 | [OMS INT](https://app.contentful.com/spaces/u9kb6gp6slxu/environments/sit/views/entries) | `sit` | `npm run push:sit` | zimmermann-sit.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 5 | [UAT](https://app.contentful.com/spaces/u9kb6gp6slxu/environments/uat/views/entries) | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 6 | [STAGE](https://app.contentful.com/spaces/u9kb6gp6slxu/environments/staging/views/entries) | `staging` | `npm run push:staging` | zimmermann-stg.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | [PRODUCTION](https://app.contentful.com/spaces/u9kb6gp6slxu/views/entries) | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Per env, server-side only | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| `fr` | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |
| `it` | Italian | ZimmermannEUit | en |
| `es` | Spanish | ZimmermannEUes | en |
| `en-CH` | English (EU International) | ZimmermannEUIntl | en |
| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |
| **Deploy** | `npm run sync:contentful` or migration | Imported at runtime — no push step |
| **Current types** | shoppableImage | CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage |

### Migration format

export const id = '002-my-change';

// Use the contentful-management plain client

Drift Detection & Promotion Rules
---------------------------------

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.
* **Migration runner** calls `detectDrift` automatically before applying. Use `--force` to bypass.

Scripts Reference

content.text:
Full analysis complete, cross-referencing the current v38 TSD against the live runbook (v10). Found two genuine, previously-unflagged misalignments (one of them is actually an internal contradiction in our own TSD), one imprecision, one ambiguity that exists in the parent itself, and one place where the "misalignment" runs the other way (the parent is stale, we're not).

## 1. Internal contradiction in our own TSD, surfaced by the runbook's precise data (highest severity)

Our **§2.1 Constraints** states as settled fact: *"Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI."*

The runbook's **Scripts Reference table** says the opposite about who runs it: `npm run sync:contentful` → **"Any developer."** Not CI at all for this script (contrast: `migrate:contentful` and `detect:drift` are listed as "CI / developer" — both — but `sync:contentful` specifically is developer-only).

This also **contradicts our own Appendix B**, which lists *"wire sync/migrate/drift into CI"* as still **Incomplete**. So §2.1 asserts CI-driven deployment as an existing constraint, while Appendix B says that CI wiring hasn't happened yet — two sections of the same document disagree. Checking back against the original v30 source, the "via CI" phrasing was **added during our reformat** (the original just said "deployed via `npm run sync:contentful`," without claiming who runs it) — this looks like an error we introduced, not one we inherited.

## 2. A §7 risk row that Tim already resolved, and we never removed

§7 still carries: *"Contentful Enterprise plan required for the production alias; unconfirmed... Confirm the account tier before first production release. Owner: Zimmermann."*

But Tim already confirmed this directly, in his own comment on this TSD (the one we resolved as item #4: *"this row isn't needed, they are on the enterprise plan"*). We removed the duplicate assumption row in §2.2, but this parallel risk row in §7 was never touched and still frames it as an open, unconfirmed question. Worth noting: the runbook itself doesn't independently confirm Zimmermann's enrollment either, it only states the alias mechanism's prerequisite (*"The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan"*) — the actual confirmation exists only in Tim's comment, so this §7 row is now stale specifically because of something Tim told us, not something the runbook resolves.

## 3. Token-boundary imprecision

Our **§5.5 Token boundary table** describes CMA scope as *"CI host only."* The runbook documents a second, legitimate use the TSD doesn't mention: a **"Per-developer setup"** section stating *"Each developer generates their own CMA token... Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`."* So CMA isn't CI-only; it's also a personal, per-developer local token. The underlying security claim in our TSD ("never in MRT/bundle") still holds either way, so this is a precision gap, not a security error.

## 4. An ambiguity that exists in the parent doc itself (not something we introduced, but worth flagging)

The runbook's **Environment Topology table** numbers tiers as: DEV(1-2), TEST(3), OMS INT/sit(4), **UAT(5)**, **STAGE(6)**, PRODUCTION(7). But the runbook's own **"Promotion order"** line right below says: *"dev → test → sit → **staging** → **uat** → master"* — staging before UAT, the opposite of the table's numbering. Our TSD's §2.1 (*"dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production"*) matches the runbook's prose line, but not its table. So we're consistent with one part of our source and inconsistent with another part of that same source, because the source disagrees with itself.

## 5. Where the parent is actually stale, not us (worth knowing, not a TSD fix)

The runbook's **Content Type Management table** documents Studio Experience definitions as living at `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` — a per-component naming pattern. That doesn't match the actual codebase (a single generated `definitions.ts`, produced via `defineComponents` + `npm run generate:contentful`) — which is exactly what our TSD's §5.5 correctly describes. This is the runbook being out of date relative to the code, not our TSD being wrong. (Side note, consistent with an earlier finding this session: the CI drift-audit job also still scans for the runbook's stale `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` pattern and matches nothing as a result.)

## One positive confirmation, not a misalignment

The runbook states a general field-localization convention: *"All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`."* Our Option A design (`sfccCategoryId`/`sfccProductId` as `localized: false`) follows this pre-existing convention exactly — it's not something we invented, it's consistent with an already-established Zimmermann rule. Worth citing as supporting evidence for Option A if that ever comes up again.

1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.

### 1.2 Problem

Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.
2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.
3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined.
4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners.
5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy.

*These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.*

---

2. Constraints & Assumptions
----------------------------

### 2.1 Constraints

| Constraint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. |
| Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |
| Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). |
| Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions applied via npm run sync:contentful. Run manually by a developer today, not yet wired into CI (see Appendix B); never hand-created in the Contentful UI. |
| Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. |
| Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. |

### 2.2 Assumptions

| Assumption | Risk if Wrong |
| --- | --- |
| Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. |

Whether the Contentful locale count also rises from 9 to 10 is genuinely undecided: it could reuse `en-US`, or get its own locale (most likely `en-CA`, matching the precedent set by the other Global-e-owned sites `en-CH`/`en-HK`/`en-AE`, each of which has its own distinct locale). This is a known, already-tracked item (`.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md`), not new. Confirm the locale choice and rollout timing with the regional-config owner before Contentful's environment/locale bootstrap. See Section 7. |
| Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. |

---

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) |
| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |
| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.

#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)

Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.

#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*

Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.

---

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**

### 4.2 Rationale

Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.
* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).

---

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)

1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).
2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).
3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.
4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.
5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).
6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).
7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.

> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.

### 5.2 Component / API Changes

| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |
| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |
| `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | Add `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` ShortText (`type: 'Symbol'`, `localized: false`) fields to ID-targeted content types; add all Sprint 1/2 content types (Appendix C). | New / Modified |
| `overrides/app/components/contentful/*` and `experiences/*` | One typed, presentation-only React component per content type (see the Studio-versus-coded rule, 5.5). | New / Modified |
| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |

> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.

### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces

**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):

| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |
| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |
| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):

`{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: [],
}`

**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**

`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({
content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',
locale: currentLocale,
});
const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {
const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;
// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render
return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;
});
// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component
return matchedInserts;`

**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.

**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.

### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |
| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |
| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case |

> **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7.

### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes

**Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7.

**Token boundary.**

| Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI service account, and each developer's own local `.env` | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Personal per-developer tokens for local work; a separate CI service-account token for automation. Never in MRT or the browser bundle. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). |

**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:

* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.
* **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.
* **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.
* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.

---

6. Testing & Validation
-----------------------

### 6.1 Test Coverage

This spike produces findings and a design, not a testable build; the tests below belong to the downstream build stories.

| Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validation of findings (this spike) | The design cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence (maps to Section 1.4). | Every design claim traces to a verified source; current-versus-target state is stated honestly. |
| Unit (downstream) | SSR-side SFCC-ID filter; presentation-only component renders pre-filtered entries and null-returns on empty. | Filter selects matching + null-ID entries only; component holds no ID logic. |
| Integration (downstream) | SSR cache key includes the SFCC ID; publish webhook purges the correct keys. | No cross-page editorial bleed; content updates appear after publish within the SWR window. |
| E2E / Playwright (downstream) | Editorial content renders on the scoped category/product page and not elsewhere. | Observable in the UI across representative storefronts. |

### 6.2 Regression Risk

Low today: the reformatted design does not change running code. The material regression surface arrives with the downstream build, concentrated on two points that the build stories must cover explicitly: **SSR ID-filter correctness** and **cache-key isolation** (a wrong or missing key leaks editorial content across pages).

content.text:
Good, found something concrete to ground this in, not just "common sense."

## Where these cons come from, and what they mean

**Con #1: "SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages."**

ELI5: Picture two shoppers, one browsing "Dresses," one browsing "Shirts." Both category pages might show a Contentful-authored banner. If we cache the server-rendered response to save work, and that cache doesn't know "this saved copy is *for* Dresses, that one is *for* Shirts," it can accidentally hand the Dresses banner to the Shirts page, or vice versa. The fix is: bake the category/product ID into the cache's storage key, so a Dresses-page cache entry and a Shirts-page cache entry are never confused for each other.

Where it's from: this isn't a fact someone looked up, it's a basic, well-known caching rule ("the cache key must include everything that changes what's inside the response"), applied to this specific pattern. But it's not just abstract theory either, I checked, and this exact principle is **already proven and already in use today**: `01-sfcc.md:93` documents the existing SFCC edge cache: *"cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group."* Option A's con is just saying: add one more thing to that same list, the SFCC category/product ID. It's not a new risky idea, it's the same pattern the system already relies on, extended by one dimension.

**Con #2: "Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct."**

ELI5: Option A puts ALL the "does this content belong on this page?" decision-making in one shared place (the SSR layer), instead of scattering it across every individual component. Good: one place to get it right, consistent everywhere. Bad: if that one shared place has a bug, every content type using this pattern breaks at the same time, not just one isolated component.

Where it's from: also a basic software truism, centralizing logic always trades "consistency" for "single point of failure." It's true by definition, not something SFCC-specific. Tim's actual complaint wasn't "prove this," it was "what do we mean by this," the sentence is just too vague as written, it doesn't say what breaking looks like.

## Confirmation status, and what's needed

**Neither con is, or can be, empirically tested right now.** Both describe a mechanism (the SSR-first fetch) that doesn't exist in code yet, there's nothing to run and check. Both are "this will be true once built, if built correctly" statements, not "this is true today" statements. That's the honest answer to Tim's "verified or a Claude assumption" question, it's neither, it's a design consequence.

- **Con #1:** Backed by real precedent (`01-sfcc.md:93`), not invented. What's needed: reword to say plainly it's a design requirement (not a tested fact, since the mechanism isn't built), and cite the existing SFCC cache-key precedent so it reads as "consistent with how this system already works" rather than a bare assertion. Nobody outside us needs to weigh in, this is a documentation-clarity fix we can do ourselves.
- **Con #2:** True by definition, just too vague. What's needed: reword to name the actual failure mode (a bug in the shared filter breaks every ID-targeted content type at once, not just one), so the sentence answers "what do we mean" instead of leaving it open.

SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation\\n-------------------------------\\n\\n### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)\\n\\nAll product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.\\n\\n#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type\\n\\nPWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.\\n\\n| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |\\n| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |\\n| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |\\n\\nThe \\\"SSR shell + CSR data\\\" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.\\n\\n### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang\\n\\nCanonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.\\n\\n### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots\\n\\nPer-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.\\n\\n### 8.4 Structured data\\n\\nCustom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:\\n\\n* **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.\\n* **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).\\n* **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.\\n* **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).\\n\\n### 8.5 URL strategy\\n\\n* Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.\\n* Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.\\n* 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.\\n\\n### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)\\n\\nNo GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.\\n\\n---\\n\\n9. Performance Strategy\\n-----------------------\\n\\nLCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.\\n\\n| Metric | Target |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |\\n| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |\\n| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |\\n| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |\\n\\n### 9.1 Third-party defer rule\\n\\nAnything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.\\n\\n### 9.2 Other levers\\n\\n* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.\\n* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:\\n\\n  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.\\n  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.\\n  + Across both: `preload=\\\"metadata\\\"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.\\n* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.\\n* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.\\n\\n### 9.3 Where performance is measured\\n\\nThe CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.\\n\\n> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.\\n\\n---\\n\\n10. Graceful Degradation\\n------------------------\\n\\nEach external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.\\n\\n| System | Failure mode |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |\\n| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |\\n| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |\\n| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |\\n| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |\\n| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |\\n| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |\\n| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |\\n\\n### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment\\n\\nThe failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.\\n\\n#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)\\n\\n* **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.\\n* **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.\\n\\n#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)\\n\\n`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).\\n\\n> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.\\n\\nThe connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):\\n\\n| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `sfcc-scapi` | `<https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`> | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |\\n| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |\\n| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |\\n| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `<https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |\\n| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `<https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |\\n| `google-places` | `<https://places.googleapis.com`> (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |\\n| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |\\n\\n**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).\\n\\n---\\n\\n13. Testing Strategy\\n--------------------\\n\\nThree layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.\\n\\n| Layer | Tool | Covers |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |\\n| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |\\n| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |\\n\\n### 13.1 What is tested\\n\\nFailure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.\\n\\n### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow\\n\\nEvery Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.\\n\\n### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures\\n\\nE2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 8 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)\\n\\n### 13.4 Selector priority\\n\\nTests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.\\n\\n---\\n\\n14. PR-only |\\n\\nRelease branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.\\n\\n### 14.3 CI workflows\\n\\n**QA workflow (**`qa.yml`) — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:\\n\\n* Unit tests (Vitest)\\n* Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)\\n\\n**SIT gate (**`digital-sit.yml`) — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:\\n\\n* Playwright `p0` priority specs\\n* Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9\\n* Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification\\n* Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)\\n* Trend gate against the LHCI history server\\n\\n### 14.4 Deployment\\n\\nDeployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:\\n\\n* **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)\\n* **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)\\n* **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties\\n* **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off\\n* **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions\\n\\nProduction deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.\\n\\nMRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.\"\n  }\n}"}

==============================================

*Last updated 2026-07-16. Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet.*

---

1. Purpose & Scope
------------------

This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at <http://www.zimmermann.com> — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.

**In scope:**

* Stack and build pipeline
* The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
* Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 8 storefronts in 6 regions
* Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
* SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
* Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
* Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
* Open decisions requiring client input before build

**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

---

2. Solution Overview
--------------------

A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

Legend / boundaries:

* **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, Narvar Promise, Adyen Drop-In, Measmerize:** browser-direct; no SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, and Narvar Promise load post-Didomi-consent only.
* **PWA → Google Maps, GiveX balance check, MuleSoft (select direct calls), Booxi:** MRT-mediated — called from the Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/`; credentials held as MRT environment variables, never in the browser bundle.
* **PWA → SFCC:** all commerce data (catalogue, cart, pricing, customer, orders) via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.
* **SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore / AP21 / Omneo / Narvar:** write and sync flows initiated by SFCC.
* **AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (inbound):** product and pricing master feed into the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks.
* **Omneo iFrame (My Account):** also surfaced as a browser-direct iFrame in My Account (CRM-176); all other Omneo traffic via MuleSoft.
* **PWA (MRT) → MuleSoft → NewStore:** read flows — order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check. SFCC is not in this path.
* **SFCC server-side integrations (cartridge-based unless noted):** Avalara, Adyen server API, GiveX (via NewStore adapter).
* **Global-e (two surfaces):** (1) browser handoff iframe at checkout for international orders (PAY-054); (2) server-side pricing/catalogue feed into SFCC (PRC-34..43).

---

3. Frontend Stack
-----------------

### 3.1 Bundled by PWA Kit

| Layer | Library | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base framework | PWA Kit on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 | Current baseline |
| UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme tokens |
| Routing | React Router v6 |  |
| Server / async state | TanStack Query via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` | All SFCC data fetching |
| i18n | react-intl | Translations under `translations/` |
| Build / dev | Webpack 5 via `pwa-kit-dev` |  |

### 3.2 Project additions

| Layer | Library | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type safety | TypeScript strict mode | All custom code is `.ts` / `.tsx` |
| Component explorer | Storybook 8 + `@storybook/addon-a11y` | `play` functions for interaction tests |
| Unit testing | Vitest (+ `vitest-axe`) | Project-level test runner |
| E2E | Playwright (+ `axe-playwright`) | Multi-region fixtures from day one |
| Forms | react-hook-form + zod | Introduced when checkout / account work begins |
| Global UI state | Zustand | Per-request store in SSR |

---

4. Customisation Model
----------------------

This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's *template extensibility* model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.

All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.

**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.

**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.

### 4.1 Environment Configuration

All secrets and per-tier identifiers are injected as **Managed Runtime environment variables**. Unless public identifiers, they must never be committed to source control or exposed in client-side bundles. The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. The table below shows the groups so each credential's boundary is clear.

| Group | Purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMMERCE_API_*`, `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` | SFCC SCAPI / SLAS client config | Browser-direct (public client ID) + MRT-mediated (token refresh) |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` | Google Maps Places API (address autocomplete) | MRT-mediated — key never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Contentful Delivery API (published content) | Browser + SSR. CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_HOST` | Contentful Preview API (drafts, editor sessions) | MRT-mediated — proxied server-side; never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Contentful Management API (schema sync) | **Local / CI only** — never deployed to MRT |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Shared secret for the Contentful → MRT cache-purge webhook (HMAC verification) | MRT-mediated |
| `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | PWA → MuleSoft direct calls (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`): order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock, GiveX balance | MRT-mediated — credentials never reach the browser |
| `ADYEN_CLIENT_KEY`, `ADYEN_ENVIRONMENT` | Adyen Drop-In / Components SDK at checkout (tokenisation, 3DS2 inline). Server-side `/payments` calls and HMAC live in SFCC BM | Browser-direct — client key is public by design (PAY-021) |
| `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` | Inside Chat support widget. **Likely NOT PWA-owned** — Inside Chat loads via GTM script injection through the Addingwell container (HPC-039/040), so its token sits inside the GTM container config (Tell No Lies), not a PWA env var. Retain only if the PWA must initialise the widget itself; confirm with Tell No Lies | Browser-direct — public token (if used at all) |
| `NARVAR_ACCOUNT_ID` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD widget at checkout (domestic only) | Browser-direct — public ID |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 site key (registration / login forms) | Browser-direct — public site key only |
| `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 secret key — used by the MRT layer to verify tokens against Google's `siteverify` endpoint; never reaches the browser | MRT-mediated |
| `GLOBALE_*` | Global-e merchant ID, environment, script host, supported countries, server-side API key | Browser-direct (script host, merchant ID) + MRT-mediated (API key, if used) — final shape pending PRC-34..43 sign-off |
| `DIDOMI_API_KEY` | Didomi Notice/Consent ID | Browser-direct — public ID, safe in bundle |
| `GTM_CONTAINER_ID`, `GTM_SERVER_URL` | GTM container and Addingwell first-party tagging-server hostname (`<https://ruffles.zimmermann.com`).> The loader uses both: `${GTM_SERVER_URL}/gtm.js?id=${GTM_CONTAINER_ID}` | Browser-direct — both public, safe in bundle. One pair per environment |
| `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY`, `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` | Observability | MRT-mediated (license keys held server-side); `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (one of `local`, `dev`, `sit`, `stage`, `uat`, `prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry / New Relic / GTM |
| `MARKETING_CLOUD_*`, `COMMERCE_AGENT_SETTINGS`, `OTP_TOKEN_LENGTH` | PWA Kit base-template defaults referenced by the base runtime configuration | Likely removable once email/auth wiring is finalised (Zimmermann uses Emarsys via Omneo, not Marketing Cloud) |

**Security policy:**

* Real values live only in local, untracked environment files — one shared file (`.env.shared`, tier-independent) plus one per deployment tier (`.env.<tier>` for dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). Only a template — variable names tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on their own comment line, no secret values — is committed to source control as `.env.sample`. Two guardrails enforce this: a pre-commit hook that blocks commit if `.env.sample` contains a secret-shaped non-empty value, and a Claude Code rule that instructs the AI assistant never to write real secret values into `.env.sample`.
* Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
* Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
* Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
* MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

---

5. Multi-Site, Multi-Locale Architecture
----------------------------------------

### 5.1 Storefronts

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions**, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods. 11 active locales total. US/EU domestic and international are configured as separate SFCC sites (REG-006).

| Locale | URL prefix | Currency | Checkout owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AU + Oceania | `/` (x-default hreflang) | AUD | SFCC (REG-003) |
| UK | `/uk/` | GBP | SFCC (REG-004) |
| US domestic | `/us/` | USD | SFCC (REG-005) |
| US international | `/en-ca/` | USD | Global-e (REG-005) |
| EU domestic — EN / FR / IT / ES | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR | SFCC (REG-006 dom) |
| EU international | `/en-ch/` | EUR | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK | `/hk/` | HKD (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-007) |
| ME | `/en-ae/` | AED (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-008) |

Rest-of-world traffic routes via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` (DMU-013). AU is configured at the root with no locale prefix and serves as the x-default hreflang target (DMU-016).

### 5.2 Entry routing

* **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
* **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
* **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.

### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale

Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.

### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed

* **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
* **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
* **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
* **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.

### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

* **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
* **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
* **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
* **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

---

6. Checkout Ownership Branching
-------------------------------

Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.

* **SFCC owns:** AU domestic (including Oceania — Avalara for NZ + New Caledonia), UK, US (when shipping to US), EU domestic.
* **Global-e owns:** HK, ME, EU international, the US site when shipping outside the US, and any domestic storefront when the selected shipping destination is outside that storefront's market.
* **Pricing for Global-e markets (REG-041):** SFCC holds all pricebooks (including Global-e ones), derived nightly from AP21 base prices and Global-e FX/coefficients. SFCC sends the complete cart in target currency at handoff; Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from that point. Full mechanism specified under PRC-34..43.
* **Global-e shipping country lock (REG-028):** locked at the country selector pre-checkout; cannot change once inside Global-e.

---

7. Integration Map
------------------

### 7.1 Classification model

Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.

* **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
* **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
* **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
* **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
* **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).

A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.

> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

### 7.2 Integration map

| System | Role | Call origin | Hosting layer | Security |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| **Contentful — Delivery (CDA)** | Published editorial content (on live website) | MRT + Browser | Browser-direct + MRT-mediated | CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle. SSR-first for SEO/LCP, browser hydration uses the SSR payload |
| **Contentful — Preview (CPA)** | Editor preview sessions, draft content | MRT (SSR pass and editor proxy) | MRT-mediated | CPA token is semi-sensitive (exposes drafts); held server-side and proxied through MRT — never reaches the browser |
| **Contentful — Management (CMA)** | Schema sync (`npm run sync:contentful`), Studio editor OAuth | Out-of-band (CI host) | Out-of-band | CMA token never embedded; stored as a CI environment variable on the host that runs the sync |
| **Contentful publish webhook** | Cache invalidation on entry publish | Contentful → MRT | MRT-mediated | Webhook receiver in the Node/SSR layer; shared-secret HMAC verification on the incoming request |
| **Vimeo** | Product video hosting — PDP gallery, runway / campaign clips (PRD-066/067) | Browser (lazy iframe embed) | Browser-direct | Embed URL stored in product data or the CMS; no secret. 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
-------------------------------

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)

All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type

PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.

| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang

Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots

Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data

Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:

* **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
* **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
* **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
* **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy

* Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
* Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
* 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)

No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

9. Performance Strategy
-----------------------

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers

* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:

  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  + Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.
